title: ROOT CAUSE of the lost Windows marker: Vencord's own persistAfterDiscordUpdates hook, bundled inside Subline's mod, copies the stub (never the marker) into every new app-1.0.x folder
file: /Users/surfer/dev/Vencord/src/main/persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts (lines 53-70, bundled via /Users/surfer/dev/Vencord/src/main/patcher.ts lines 49-52); consumer: /Users/surfer/dev/discord-translate/installer/src/patcher/state.ts classifyStub lines 251-313
scenario: 1. Subline patched app-1.0.9258 (stub + marker + _app.asar). 2. Discord downloads 1.0.9259 into a fresh app-1.0.9259 (helper logs it unpatched, deferred because Discord is running). 3. User quits Discord. Vencord's main-process code (running from Subline's patcher.js) fires on app 'before-quit', finds the newer folder, renames its app.asar to _app.asar and copyFileSync's the OLD folder's app.asar (Subline's stub, byte for byte) over it. It copies nothing else: no subline-patch.json. 4. Next helper run: stub loads %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline\mod\patcher.js, marker null, so classifyStub takes the foreign branch; identifyModFromLoaderPath sees no 'vencord' substring and answers 'unknown' = 'another client mod'. Helper logs foreign-mod and abandons; uninstall refuses FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT. Evidence in ~/Desktop/diagnostics.txt: line 194 (app-1.0.9256 unpatched 2026-09-03) -> line 476 (same folder patched-by-other 2026-09-08) with no Subline write in between; again lines 1488 -> 1530 for 9259 and 1538 -> 1545 for 9260. The same mechanism explains the 2026-09-02 'two siblings both patched' brick noted in locate.ts.
whatHappens: Every Windows Discord host update produces an own-loader stub with no marker. Until the ownership fix lands the helper abandons the install and uninstall fails; after the fix the hook still (a) propagates whatever stub bytes the old folder had, including pre-0.2.1 one-line stubs that crash Discord when the bundle is gone, (b) writes to Discord's folder from inside Discord with no settle/quiet guard and no Subline log line, and (c) leaves _app.asar + stub in a folder Subline has never recorded, so helper memory and patched-installs.json never learn about it. `if (process.env.DISABLE_UPDATER_AUTO_PATCHING) return;` cannot be set from outside Discord.
fix: Own this behaviour in the build rather than suffer it: in scripts/buildMod.mjs apply a source patch to persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts so that when it repatches the newer folder it (1) copies subline-patch.json alongside app.asar and (2) writes the current fail-open stub via the same bytes rather than copying whatever the old folder holds; or replace the require in patcher.ts with Subline's own persist module that does exactly that. Keep the in-progress classifyStub fix as defence in depth (a stub whose loader is this account's bundle loader is ours, marker or not), so a hook from any Vencord build still classifies correctly. Add the marker copy to docs/RELEASING.md as a build invariant.
test: Build-level: tests/bundle.test.ts asserts the built patcher.js contains the Subline persist code (string match on 'subline-patch.json' inside the before-quit handler) and not the upstream copy-only version. State-level (win32 fixture): old folder app-1.0.1 with our stub+marker+backup, new folder app-1.0.2 with a real asar; run the extracted persist function (or replicate its writes: rename app.asar->_app.asar, copy stub, no marker) then inspectInstall(app-1.0.2) must be patched-by-us; runHelperOnce must write the marker (repatched, marker.loaderPath set); uninstallTargets+uninstall must restore BOTH folders to byte-identical originals and report clean. These fail on main.
betterFix: Keep the branch's loader-based ownership (ownership.ts isSublineLoaderPath, classifyStub marker-missing/marker-mismatch, helper re-adopt via adoptPatch) as the primary fix. It is the layer that works for any stub bytes and any Vencord pin. Do not copy subline-patch.json verbatim in the hook. The marker holds backupPath, discordVersion and patchedAt for the OLD folder. Uninstall is safe (it uses install.backupPath, not marker.backupPath), but the helper's version-changed check would read a stale discordVersion, and the marker would lie about where the backup is. If a build-level change is wanted, do this instead: 1. In installer/scripts/buildMod.mjs use the existing exactly-once replace mechanism (the one that rewrites settings.tsx) on persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts so the hook writes a FRESH marker after copyFileSync: discordVersion from the new folder's build_info.json, backupPath = the new _app.asar, pluginBuildId from subline-mod.json beside patcher.js, patchedAt = now, format 2. Fail the build if the find string is absent, so a pin change cannot silently drop it. 2. Add to tests/bundle.test.ts: the built patcher.js contains "Detected Host Update" and the _app.asar guard, so a future pin without upstream's #4472 fix fails the build. 3. Leave the copied stub bytes alone. The copied stub is the one that just booted this Discord. A legacy stub is rewritten by the helper's next build-changed repatch, and Windows Discord is per-user, so the unreadable-loader crash does not arise there. 4. In docs/RELEASING.md record that Windows survives host updates because of this hook, and that the helper must re-adopt any own-loader stub without a marker. Also cover the neighbour: a crash between patch.ts line 377 (stub in place) and line 395 (marker written) leaves the same marker-less own stub; the branch's ownership fix covers it, so add a test that kills the write between those two steps and expects patched-by-us plus re-adopt.

title: Uninstall removes the helper before it knows the restore can succeed, so every failed uninstall orphans an install the helper owned
scenario: 1. ipcMain uninstall:run computes targets and the permission probe, then calls removeHelperFor (task/LaunchAgent deleted) BEFORE uninstall() inspects anything. 2. uninstall() then gets FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (field case, diagnostics lines 1594-1602), BACKUP_MISSING, BACKUP_CORRUPT or FILE_IN_USE from unpatch. 3. Report: helperStopped true but summary 'Nothing has been deleted, so Discord keeps working exactly as it does now'. The second attempt in the field logged helperRemoved=false because the task was already gone. 4. Subline keeps loading in Discord with no helper: the next Discord update (new folder on Windows, in-place on macOS) ends translation silently and no process repairs it; the user believes they are mid-uninstall.
whatHappens: Product rule 'the helper must never abandon an install it owns' is broken by the uninstaller itself, and the summary is false about what changed.
fix: Dry-run first: inspectInstall every target before removing the helper; if any target would refuse (broken unrecoverable, foreign with our marker mismatch, not-writable) return the exact reason with nothing changed. If a restore still fails after the helper was removed, re-register the helper (installHelperFor / ensureHelper) and say so in the summary ('Background repair was turned back on'). Make the summary read helperStopped rather than claiming nothing changed.
test: uninstall.test.ts: with an unpatch port that fails for one target, assert the helper-removal port was not called (dry-run refusal) or that a re-register port was called and the summary mentions it; assert no summary contains 'Nothing has been deleted' when helperStopped is true. Fails on main.
betterFix: 1. Move the whole ordering into app/uninstall.ts so it is testable. Replace the `helper: HelperRemoval` precondition with ports: `dryRun(install)`, `removeHelper()`, `reinstallHelper()`. Make uninstall() async. main.ts then only supplies the ports. 2. Order inside uninstall(): (a) DISCORD_RUNNING check, (b) dry run of every target, (c) removeHelper, (d) unpatch every target, (e) if any restore failed and helper.removed was true, call reinstallHelper and record the result, (f) bundle and settings as today. 3. The dry run must be unpatchInstall itself, not a hand-written inspect. Add `dryRun: true` to UnpatchOptions: run inspectInstall with ownLoaderPaths, the backup existence check and readIsOriginalAsar on _app.asar, and return the exact error it would return, before any renameSync. Two inspection paths drift; one cannot. 4. Summaries must read what happened. Pass helper.removed and helperReinstalled into summarize(). When the helper was removed and put back: "Background repair was turned back on." When it was removed and could not be put back: say so and name the fix (run the installer again). Delete the sentence "Nothing has been deleted/changed" from any branch reachable after removeHelper. 5. main.ts: move quitDiscord and listProcesses above the uninstall() call as today, but removeHelperFor goes into the port and is no longer called inline. 6. Field recovery for machines already in this state: on app launch, if patched-installs.json names an install whose stub loads our loader and no task/plist is registered, re-register via installHelperFor and log helper.readopted. The user's item 3 (helper re-adopts and rewrites the marker) needs a helper that exists. Tests (uninstall.test.ts, must fail on main): dry run returns FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT for one of two targets -> removeHelper port never called, nothing unpatched, summary names the mod; dry run passes but unpatch fails with FILE_IN_USE -> reinstallHelper called, summary contains "turned back on", helperStopped false; discordRunning non-empty -> removeHelper never called; no report with helper.removed true may contain "Nothing has been" unless reinstall succeeded; patch.test.ts: dryRun true leaves app.asar, _app.asar and the marker byte-identical and returns the same code the real call returns.

title: Uninstall fails and tells the user 'could not fully remove itself' whenever ANY swept Discord (Canary with Vencord, a Vencord-owned live Stable while Subline is on a hand-picked PTB) belongs to another mod
scenario: 1. User has Subline on Stable and Vencord on Canary (common in the target audience), or Vencord on Stable and Subline on a hand-picked PTB. 2. Uninstall: uninstallTargets adds every live install plus every folder of every branch where carriesOurMark is true, and carriesOurMark is 'exists(_app.asar) OR exists(marker)'. Vencord's own _app.asar qualifies, so the Vencord Canary is a target. 3. unpatchInstall on it returns FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT ('Subline is not installed here. Vencord is. Remove it with its own uninstaller.'). 4. uninstall(): restores.every(ok) is false -> discordRestored false -> bundle kept, product folder kept, summary 'Subline could not fully remove itself from Discord. Nothing has been deleted' although every Subline patch was restored. Helper was already removed at main.ts:606. Same outcome on a retry, forever. A stale Subline marker under a foreign stub (Vencord installed over us; patch.ts never removes our marker in that branch) keeps the folder a target for the same reason.
whatHappens: Uninstall never reports clean on a machine that has any other client mod anywhere; the bundle and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline are left behind; the summary is false. The user cannot tell whether Subline is gone.
fix: In uninstall(), treat a FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT result for a target whose state carries no marker of ours (or whose marker loader does not match the stub) as 'not ours': restores entry {ok: true, restored: false, skipped: 'foreign'}, logged, not a problem, not a bundle-keeper. Narrow carriesOurMark to 'marker exists' OR 'stub loader is this account's bundle loader'. When our marker sits under a foreign stub, remove the marker (provably stale) and report not ours.
test: uninstall.test.ts: two fixtures, Stable patched-by-us and Canary with a Vencord stub + Vencord _app.asar, real unpatchInstall -> report.clean true, modBundleRemoved true, Canary app.asar and _app.asar bytes unchanged, summary says Discord was put back to normal. locate.test.ts: uninstallTargets/locatePatchedResidue returns the Vencord Canary only if it carries our marker. Both fail on main.
betterFix:
Keep the broad sweep; do NOT narrow carriesOurMark. An interrupted patch (crash between step 2 and 3 of applyPatch) leaves `_app.asar` + temp file, no app.asar and no marker; "marker OR stub loader is ours" cannot see a stub that does not exist and would drop exactly the folder that needs repair. Fix the classification instead, at the point that can see the state:

1. unpatchInstall, case patched-by-other without removeForeignMod: return ok, not an error: `{restored:false, alreadyClean: marker===null, foreignMod: state.mod, removedArtifacts:[marker if it existed], summary:"<Mod> is installed here, not Subline. It was left as it is."}`. Remove our marker there: the stub is what Discord runs and it loads someone else's loader, so the marker is stale by definition, and leaving it keeps stillMarked (rememberedResources) true forever. Keep `_app.asar`: the foreign stub still boots from it. Add `foreignMod: KnownMod | null` to UnpatchReport. Update patch.test.ts:620 and foreignMarker.test.ts expectations accordingly (removeForeignMod:true path unchanged).

2. uninstall(): the bundle must stay only while some Discord still has a stub that loads OUR bundle. A failed target blocks bundle removal only when it is ours: our marker exists beside it (check existsSync(join(resourcesPath, MARKER_FILENAME)) yourself; broken() returns marker:null even when one is on disk), or the stub's loader is Subline's (isSublineLoaderPath / ownLoaderPaths). A BROKEN_INSTALL with asar-inaccessible/asar-unreadable on a target with no marker and an unreadable stub (Vencord's app.asar folder) is "not ours: skipped", logged with the reason, and does not keep the bundle. A live target of ours whose restore fails (PERMISSION_DENIED, BACKUP_MISSING, FILE_IN_USE) still keeps the bundle, unchanged. Add `skipped: "foreign" | null` to RestoreOutcome and name the skipped Discords in the summary ("Vencord on Discord Canary was left alone; it is not Subline's.").

3. Thread ownLoaderPaths into the classification used by uninstall (main.ts already computes loaderPathFor(modDir)).

Tests (all fail on main and on fix-foreign-marker today): (a) the finding's two; (b) Canary app.asar as a directory with index.js + package.json and _app.asar -> clean=true, folder untouched; (c) Stable with a Vencord stub over a stale Subline marker -> marker removed, _app.asar and stub bytes unchanged, clean=true; (d) Windows: older app-x sibling with our stub and no marker is still restored (guards the 2026-09-02 brick); (e) interrupted patch (`_app.asar` only) is still repaired; (f) live Stable ours with a PERMISSION_DENIED restore plus a foreign Canary -> bundle kept, summary names the real failure, not the Canary.

title: Stub pointing at a missing or throwing loader: the helper neither repairs nor alerts, the installer says 'installed', and legacy (and Vencord-copied) one-line stubs stop Discord starting
scenario: A. Bundle gone or corrupt (AV quarantines %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline\mod\renderer.js or truncates patcher.js, user deletes the Subline folder, a failed uninstall that kept the bundle followed by a manual delete, disk error). inspectInstall never checks the loader exists: state is patched-by-us, summary 'Subline is installed'. Helper: readInstalledBundle -> 'bundle-unusable' (a log line, no alert), bundle null so the reconcile loop is skipped (helper.ts:324); maybeUpdate runs, and offline or with no newer feed entry nothing is written; after three failed checks the only alert is 'Subline has not been able to check for updates'. B. The fail-open stub only guards accessSync(L): a patcher.js that exists but throws (truncated, syntax error) is required anyway and Discord's main process dies before the window opens. C. Any pre-0.2.1 one-line stub (still accepted as verified by verifyPatch:346-347, and copied forward by Vencord's hook on every Windows update) throws 'Cannot find module' as soon as the bundle is gone. Uninstall still works (restoreOriginal), but nobody is told to run it.
whatHappens: Discord does not start (B, C) or Subline silently vanishes (A) with the helper reporting nothing actionable and the installer saying all is well.
fix: stub.ts: wrap require(L) in try/catch and fall back to _app.asar when the loader throws (Vencord's patcher only changes global state after its requires succeed, so the fallback is safe). state.ts: add loaderPresent/warning 'loader-missing' to patched-by-us. helper.ts: when the bundle is unusable and an install is patched-by-us, either restore the original (unpatchInstall) when Discord is closed or rewrite the fail-open stub, and raise a 'repatch-failed' alert naming the bundle; when the bundle is fine, treat a legacy stub as 'patch-outdated' and rewrite it under the same settle gate. Installer alreadyInstalled: a missing loader is an update, not 'nothing left to do'.
test: stubFailOpen.test.ts: loader file present containing 'throw new Error("boom")' and one containing a syntax error -> exit 0 and stock Discord booted. helper.test.ts: patchForReal, delete the bundle dir, run -> an alert is raised and afterwards inspectInstall is unpatched or the stub is fail-open (run the stub in a child process as stubFailOpen does); legacy stub + valid bundle + Discord closed -> repatched and stub.indexSource === stubIndexSource(loader). state.test.ts: patched-by-us with missing loader carries the warning. All fail on main.
betterFix:
1. stub.ts: keep the accessSync branch, and wrap require(L) so the fallback runs only when the loader never got past its preamble: `try{require(L)}catch(e){if(require.main.filename!==__filename)throw e;console.error("[Subline] loader failed",e);<boot _app.asar>}`. Vencord sets require.main.filename before any side effect, so syntax errors, truncation, MODULE_NOT_FOUND inside the loader, and throws before the preamble fall back safely; a throw after Discord started is rethrown. Test both throw and syntax-error loaders in stubFailOpen.test.ts (exit 0, stock booted) and a loader that sets require.main.filename then throws (exit 1, no double boot).

2. state.ts: add `loaderPresent: boolean` and `stubForm: "fail-open" | "legacy"` to InstallState, and the warning "loader-missing" on patched-by-us when existsSync(loaderPath) is false. Do not raise it when ports.isOtherAccountLoader(loader) is true: another account's home is unreadable from here, so existsSync is false for a healthy install. Keep the kind patched-by-us so uninstall still works. Many state and foreignMarker tests use loader paths that do not exist; they need real temp loaders or an explicit warning expectation.

3. flow.ts alreadyInstalled: after the other-account check, `loader-missing` sets this.updating = true and goes to checkRunning, so the bundle is reinstalled and the stub rewritten.

4. helper.ts: when bundle is null and this run's maybeUpdate did not install one, raise a new alert code "bundle-missing" at once, naming the bundle dir: "Subline's files are missing from <dir>. Open Subline to reinstall." Do not reuse repatch-failed; its copy says "Discord updated". For a managed install whose stubForm is legacy, unpatch it under the settle gate with requireDiscordClosed on both OSes, and keep run.state.installs so the next successful feed update re-patches it (collectManaged already treats remembered installs as ours). A fail-open stub needs no write.

5. helper.ts, bundle usable, stubForm legacy: a new RepatchReason "stub-outdated" that runs applyPatch only when Discord is closed on both OSes, raises neither quit-required nor restart-required, and does not push a deferralKey. Otherwise a Windows user who never quits Discord gets "Discord updated, quit Discord" nags for a no-op, which is the reason verifyPatch accepts the legacy form today.

6. patch.ts alreadyPatched shortcut: add `state.stubForm === "fail-open"` to the condition, so an installer run (Discord is closed at that point) upgrades a legacy stub even when the build id matches.

Tests must fail on main: stubFailOpen throw/syntax cases exit 1 today; helper bundle-deleted-offline run raises no alert today; state missing loader carries no warning today; helper legacy-stub-with-valid-bundle-Discord-closed reports not-needed today.

title: The new 'own loader' predicate must be path-normalised and account-aware, or the fix fails on case/separator variants and claims another account's Subline on macOS
scenario: A (windows). The stub path comes from join(env.LOCALAPPDATA, 'Subline', 'mod', 'patcher.js') in whichever process wrote it. An installer started from a shell or launcher that sets LOCALAPPDATA as 'c:\users\x\appdata\local', forward slashes, or an 8.3 short name writes a stub that differs from the helper's string only in case or separators. An exact-string own-loader check calls it foreign again; today the exact compare already makes verifyPatch fail ('loads X instead of Y') so decideRepatch 'patch-damaged' rewrites the stub on every run where Discord is closed and raises restart-required each time (flapping). B. identifyModFromLoaderPath answers 'vencord' for any path containing 'vencord', so for a username like vencordfan Subline's own loader is reported as 'Vencord is already installed here' unless the own-loader test runs first. C (macos). /Applications/Discord.app is shared; account B's stub loads /Users/a/Library/Application Support/Subline/mod/patcher.js. The helper (isOtherAccountLoader) and the flow (otherAccount) refuse to touch it, but unpatchInstall/uninstall have no such guard: a predicate like 'ends with Subline/mod/patcher.js' or 'marker product is subline' makes B's uninstall restore Discord out from under A, report 'put back to normal', and A's helper re-patches at its next run.
whatHappens: Either the field bug returns under a different spelling of the same path, or one account removes another account's install while reporting success.
fix: Define one ownership function used by state.ts, patch.ts and uninstall: ours = marker matches stub, OR normalise(stubLoader) === normalise(thisAccountBundleLoader) where normalise on win32 lowercases, unifies separators and strips trailing separators (and resolves 8.3 names via realpath when the file exists), and on darwin uses realpath. Run it before identifyModFromLoaderPath. A loader under another account's home (isOtherAccountLoader, wired on darwin) yields kind patched-by-other with mod 'subline' and modName 'Subline (another account on this Mac)', refused by unpatch unless removeForeignMod, with that sentence in the uninstall summary.
test: state.test.ts (win32 platform injected): stub 'C:/users/X/APPDATA/local/Subline/mod/patcher.js', bundle loader 'C:\Users\X\AppData\Local\Subline\mod\patcher.js', no marker -> patched-by-us; own loader under '/Users/vencordfan/...' -> mod subline not vencord. patch.test.ts: unpatchInstall on a darwin fixture whose stub loader is '/Users/other/Library/Application Support/Subline/mod/patcher.js' (home '/Users/me') -> refused with the other-account message, bytes unchanged. helper.test.ts: the case-variant stub is 'not-needed', not repatched every run. All fail on main or on an exact-string fix.
betterFix:
Do not change state.ts classification (the proposed "patched-by-other with mod subline" kind would also change patchInstall's guard and helper outcomes). Add the guard where the write happens:

1. patch.ts UnpatchOptions: add `isOtherAccountLoader?: (loaderPath: string) => boolean`. In unpatchInstall, after inspect and before the switch: `const loader = state.marker?.loaderPath ?? state.loaderPath; if (state.kind !== "patched-by-other" && state.kind !== "unpatched" && loader && options.isOtherAccountLoader?.(loader)) return err("OTHER_ACCOUNT", "Another account on this Mac set up Subline for this Discord. Only that account can remove it. Nothing was changed.", { path: install.rootPath })`. This also covers the broken kinds (our-patch-without-backup) so B never deletes A's leftovers.
2. main.ts uninstall:run: pass the already-built port (ports.ts:717 isOtherAccountLoader, darwin only) into unpatchInstall next to ownLoaderPaths. Also skip the other-account install in `stillMarked` / bundle-kept logic in uninstall.ts so B's own bundle removal is not blocked by A's marker: treat an OTHER_ACCOUNT restore outcome as "not ours", not as a failure that keeps the bundle.
3. uninstall.ts summarize: when every problem is OTHER_ACCOUNT, return that sentence verbatim instead of "could not fully remove itself... diagnostics log".
4. Tests (fail on the branch today): patch.test.ts darwin fixture with stub loader under /Users/other, home /Users/me, marker present and absent -> error code OTHER_ACCOUNT, app.asar and _app.asar bytes unchanged, marker untouched. uninstall.test.ts: report.summary contains "Another account on this Mac", discordRestored=false, and no "put back to normal".

Optional hardening, not a bug fix: make adoptPatch (patch.ts:228) and verifyPatch (460, 498) compare with sameLoaderPath so a spelling-variant stub is re-adopted (marker only) instead of fully rewritten, which on Windows waits for Discord to close.

title: Any small archive that is not the exact two-file stub is classified 'unpatched' and patching then moves it into _app.asar as if it were Discord's original
scenario: 1. app.asar is a loader archive with a third entry (a mod that ships index.js, package.json and a LICENSE/README; a future Vencord/Equicord stub layout; a hand-written one), or a 2-file one larger than 64 KB. readStub returns null -> 'unpatched' (hasBackup only adds the stale-backup warning). 2. patchInstall: currentIsOriginal true, renameSync(app.asar, _app.asar) overwrites the real Discord backup that mod had preserved. 3. verifyPatch's readIsOriginalAsar(backup) also says 'original' (same shape test), so the patch verifies and is kept. 4. Discord starts our stub -> Subline's patcher.js -> boots _app.asar, which is the foreign stub requiring its own loader -> Discord does not start; uninstall 'restores' the foreign stub, never Discord's code.
whatHappens: The only copy of Discord's code is destroyed by a verified patch; Discord cannot start and the uninstaller cannot help (reinstall Discord is the only remedy).
fix: 'Original' needs positive evidence, not the absence of our shape: accept as original only an archive whose package.json has name 'discord' and a main under app_bootstrap/ (or whose header lists Discord's known top-level entries) and whose size is above a floor; any other archive below MAX_STUB_BYTES, or any archive with a top-level index.js that is not ours, is patched-by-other (mod unknown, loaderPath from the best-effort parse) or broken 'asar-unrecognised'. patchInstall must never rename anything but a positively identified original into _app.asar.
test: state.test.ts: 3-entry 300-byte asar (index.js requiring /opt/x, package.json, README) -> kind is not 'unpatched'. patch.test.ts: same fixture with an existing real _app.asar -> patchInstall refuses and _app.asar bytes are unchanged. Both fail on main.
betterFix: The proposed positive signature is wrong for the layout this repo already observed. The test fixtures (installer/tests/fixture.ts: buildOriginalDiscordAsar and the hand-transcribed foreignOriginalAsarBytes) record the real macOS 0.0.406 _app.asar as top-level bundle.js, package.json, splashScreenPreload.js with main 'bundle.js', not 'app_bootstrap/…'. A rule that demands main under app_bootstrap/ would call a genuine current Discord archive 'not original' and Subline could never install. A size floor alone also breaks the existing tests: the realistic-original fixtures are 393 bytes and about 4 KB. Do not hardcode Discord's file layout. Decide by what the archive's entry point does: 1) read package.json from the archive; take its main (fallback index.js); 2) if that entry is absent, or package.json is unparseable, return a new 'asar-unrecognised' broken reason (never 'unpatched'); 3) if the main entry is <= MAX_STUB_BYTES, read it and run parseRequirePath on it; a parse hit means a loader stub (loaderPath set, any entry count, any total size), so readStub returns StubContents instead of null; 4) only a main entry that exists and does not parse as a loader is 'original'. This keeps OpenAsar (large real index.js) as original, which matches what Vencord does, and classifies every require-only loader as a stub regardless of extra files. Because readIsOriginalAsar wraps readStub, verifyPatch's backup check and restoreOriginal's corrupt-backup check inherit the rule for free. Keep MAX_STUB_BYTES as the cap on the bytes read, not as the classifier. Add a belt-and-braces guard in applyPatch: when state.hasBackup is true and app.asar is about to be renamed over _app.asar, require that readStub(_app.asar) also says original; otherwise refuse with a named error rather than overwrite. Tests (must fail on main): state.test.ts: 3-entry 300-byte archive with index.js requiring /opt/x -> kind 'patched-by-other', mod 'unknown', asarIsStub true, loaderPath '/opt/x/patcher.js'; same archive with main 'loader.js' instead of index.js -> still a stub; archive with no main entry -> broken 'asar-unrecognised'. patch.test.ts: 3-entry foreign stub beside a real _app.asar -> patchInstall refuses with FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT and sha256(_app.asar) is unchanged; with overwriteForeignMod the backup bytes are still unchanged and backupCreated is false. Also assert the existing OpenAsar-like case (large multi-file archive, main index.js with real code) still reads as 'unpatched'.

title: First install from the mounted DMG or a translocated copy registers a LaunchAgent at a path that vanishes; helper never runs and 'already set up' later claims updates are handled
scenario: 1. Non-technical user double-clicks Subline.dmg and runs Subline.app from the mounted volume (or opens the quarantined app from Downloads, which macOS runs from /private/var/folders/.../AppTranslocation/.../Subline.app). 2. Install completes; installHelperFor (ports.ts:171-197) writes ProgramArguments = [/Volumes/Subline/Subline.app/Contents/MacOS/Subline, --helper] and bootstraps it. Only ensureHelperFor (ports.ts:297) and ensureHelperFromHelper (ports.ts:379) have the /Volumes and AppTranslocation guard; the install path has none. 3. The DMG is ejected or the translocation mount disappears at quit. launchd fails to spawn the job at every interval and every login. 4. title: Windows 'Uninstall' from Settings > Apps removes only Subline.exe: Discord stays patched, the scheduled task keeps firing a missing exe, and no uninstaller is left
scenario: 1. User uninstalls Subline the Windows way (Settings > Apps > Subline > Uninstall, or Control Panel). 2. electron-builder's NSIS uninstaller runs; installer.nsh defines customCheckAppRunning and customInstall but no customUnInstall, and deleteAppDataOnUninstall is false (electron-builder.js). It deletes %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\Subline only. 3. Discord's app.asar is still the stub pointing at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline\mod\patcher.js, which still exists, so Discord keeps loading Subline; \Subline\Helper still runs every 5 minutes against a deleted exe; subline-patch.json, helper-state.json and the Vencord settings stay. 4. Discord updates: Vencord's persist hook copies the stub into the new folder, so Subline survives its own uninstall indefinitely.
whatHappens: The user believes Subline is removed; Discord keeps running it, a scheduled task fires forever, and the only way to really uninstall is to download Subline again. This is the 'uninstall must always work or say exactly why' rule failing silently on the platform's own uninstall path.
fix: Add `!macro customUnInstall` to installer.nsh: run `"$INSTDIR\Subline.exe" --uninstall --keep-settings` (new headless mode in main.ts that runs the same uninstall() with helper removal and Discord-running check, writing the log) and wait; if it reports Discord running, MessageBox 'Quit Discord (check the tray near the clock) and run the uninstaller again' and Abort; always `nsExec::Exec 'schtasks /Delete /TN \Subline\Helper /F'` afterwards. Reuse the same uninstall code, never a second NSIS implementation.
test: packaging.test: installer.nsh contains `customUnInstall`, `--uninstall` and the task name from HELPER_TASK_NAME. main/ports test: the `--uninstall` entry runs uninstall() with removeHelperFor first and returns a non-zero exit when Discord is running, zero when clean.
betterFix: The proposed fix has two defects that would make it fail or do harm. (1) Wrong hook: customUnInstall is inserted at the END of Section "un.install", after `RMDir /r $INSTDIR` and after the registry keys are deleted, so `"$INSTDIR\Subline.exe" --uninstall` would run against a file that no longer exists and Abort there would leave a half-removed install with no Uninstall entry. Use `customUnInit` (runs in un.onInit, before any file is removed; the exe still exists, so ExecWait works and Abort leaves the install intact and still listed in Apps). (2) Missing update guard: on every Subline upgrade, installUtil.nsh's uninstallOldVersion runs the OLD uninstaller with `/S /KEEP_APP_DATA --updated` (lines 206, 224, 230). An unguarded hook would unpatch Discord and delete the helper task on every upgrade, and would block the upgrade whenever Discord is running. Wrap the whole hook in `${ifNot} ${isUpdated}`. Concrete shape for installer.nsh: `!macro customUnInit` -> `${ifNot} ${isUpdated}` -> `ExecWait '"$INSTDIR\Subline.exe" --uninstall --keep-settings' $0` -> if $0 == <DISCORD_RUNNING exit code> and not ${Silent}: MessageBox "Quit Discord first (check the tray near the clock), then run Uninstall again." and Abort; if $0 is any other non-zero (exe missing, crashed): do not abort, fall through so the files still go, but always `nsExec::Exec 'schtasks /Delete /TN "\Subline\Helper" /F'` as a last resort so a dead task never outlives the exe -> `${endIf}` -> `!macroend`. In main.ts add an `--uninstall` branch modelled on isHelperRun (no window, no dock, bufferedLogger, writeHeader, app.exit(code)); it must run removeHelperFor FIRST, then the same uninstall() with keepSettings from `--keep-settings`, and map UninstallReport codes to exit codes (0 clean, distinct code for DISCORD_RUNNING, another for everything else). Also exclude this flag from createWindow/ensureStartMenuShortcut exactly as isHelperRun is excluded, or the headless run restores the Start Menu shortcut the uninstaller is about to delete. Tests: packaging.test reads installer.nsh and asserts it contains customUnInit (not customUnInstall), `${ifNot} ${isUpdated}`, `--uninstall`, and the literal HELPER_TASK_NAME; a main/ports test asserts the `--uninstall` entry calls removeHelperFor before unpatch, exits non-zero on DISCORD_RUNNING, zero when clean, and never creates a window. Keep deleteAppDataOnUninstall false: the mod dir and sidecars are in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline, which that option would not touch anyway; uninstall() already removes them.

title: Windows staged update never remembers the install in patched-installs.json
scenario: 1. User with a hand-picked Discord (PTB, Canary, or an unusual folder) installed before patched-installs.json existed (added 2026-10-02, after v0.2.1). 2. They update with Discord open on Windows: stageUpdate (flow.ts:1713-1733) calls installModBundle and installHelper but never rememberPatchedInstall, which only applyPatch calls (flow.ts:1797). 3. Discord later updates. The helper's locate (helper/ports.ts:339) scans default roots for Stable only plus remembered entries, so the hand-picked install is never found; uninstallTargets finds a standard PTB through locatePatchedResidue but not an unusual folder.
whatHappens: That Discord is never repaired after its next update (silent stop) and an unusual-folder one is never found by Uninstall ('There was nothing to remove').
fix: Call this.ports.rememberPatchedInstall?.(install) in stageUpdate after a successful installModBundle, and also in alreadyInstalled for a patched-by-us install, so pre-memory installs get remembered on the first 0.2.2 run.
test: flow.test Windows staged update: remembered list contains the install after done; already-installed path with a fromExplicitPath install: remembered after the screen. Both fail on main.
betterFix:
The proposed fix is correct but incomplete in two small ways.

1. In stageUpdate, call rememberPatchedInstall right after installModBundle succeeds, inside the same try/catch applyPatch uses (flow.ts lines 1805-1809), so a failed write logs patch.remember-failed and never fails the update.

2. In alreadyInstalled, remember once, directly after the other-account guard (before the marker-missing and update-detected branches). Every later branch either ends on "already-installed" or continues into applyPatch/stageUpdate, and rememberPatchedInstall upserts by stableId, so a second write is harmless. Remembering after the other-account check matters: an install another account owns must never land in this account's memory, or Uninstall and the helper would start targeting it.

3. Neighbour to close in the same change: the installer's own locate port (installer/src/main/ports.ts line 639) does not merge readPatchedInstalls, unlike the helper's. So even a remembered hand-picked Windows install is not found by resume() or detect() on the next installer run and the user must pick the folder by hand every time. Merge remembered entries there the same way helper/ports.ts does (locateRemembered, dedupe by rootPath), and add a flow test: locate called with no explicit paths returns the remembered install and start() lands on already-installed.

Tests that fail before the fix: (a) Windows staged update with a fromExplicitPath install: remembered contains its rootPath once done is reached; (b) start() with a same-build patched-by-us install: remembered contains it after already-installed; (c) start() with an other-account install: remembered stays empty.

title: No rename retry in patch.ts: an antivirus scan of the freshly written stub fails the patch, and a second scan during rollback leaves Discord without app.asar and the flow with no repair path
scenario: Fresh install on Windows with Defender or a third-party AV doing real-time scanning. applyPatch: (1) writeFileSync(.subline-app.asar.tmp) creates a new file, the AV opens it to scan; (2) renameSync(app.asar -> _app.asar) succeeds; (3) renameSync(tmp -> app.asar) at line 253 fails EPERM/EBUSY because the AV still holds the temp; rollback(): discard(tmp) fails silently (line 431), then renameSync(_app.asar -> app.asar) at line 405. The AV's on-rename scan of _app.asar (3.6 MB, just renamed) can hold it too, so that rename also fails. Same shape as power loss between steps 2 and 3.
whatHappens: modInstall.ts got renameWithRetry for exactly this ('an antivirus scanning the fresh staging folder makes that rename fail with EPERM or EBUSY'), patch.ts did not. Case A (step 3 fails, rollback succeeds): the user sees FILE_IN_USE 'Close Discord completely, including any Discord icon in the system tray' while Discord is already closed; flaky and misleading. Case B (rollback rename also fails): ROLLBACK_FAILED. On disk app.asar is missing and _app.asar present, Discord cannot start. The patch-failed detail tells the user to move the file by hand. Pressing Try again runs patchStep -> patchInstall -> inspectInstall -> broken(asar-missing-backup-present) -> guardPatchable returns BROKEN_INSTALL (line 159). The flow's broken-install screen (flow.ts 795-803) says 'It can be repaired' but offers only retry and cancel, and retry re-detects the same state. No helper is registered yet on a fresh install, so nothing repairs it in the background. The only way out is the footer Uninstall, which does restore (unpatchBroken -> restoreOriginal), but nothing on screen says so. Product rule violated: the installer left Discord unable to start and the user stuck.
fix: (1) Move renameWithRetry out of modInstall.ts into a shared patcher module (realFs-based) and use it for the two renames in applyPatch (lines 243, 253) and the rollback rename (line 405); retry only on win32 for EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY, 100..1600 ms, same as modInstall. (2) Make patchInstall finish an interrupted patch: when state is broken with reason asar-missing-backup-present and readIsOriginalAsar(backupPath) is true, treat it as currentIsOriginal=false with no backup rename: stage the stub, rename it onto app.asar, write the marker, verify. (3) In flow.inspectChosen, for broken reasons asar-missing-backup-present and our-patch-without-backup offer a 'repair' action that calls ports.unpatch (restoreOriginal) and then re-detects; on ROLLBACK_FAILED the patch-failed detail must name that button, not a manual file move. (4) Case A's message: when Discord was confirmed closed just before the write, say 'Another program (often antivirus) is scanning Discord's files. Wait a few seconds and try again.'
test: tests/patch.test.ts with a fault-injection seam on rename: (a) win32, first rename(tmp -> app.asar) throws EPERM once then succeeds: patchInstall returns ok, app.asar is the stub, _app.asar is the original. Fails today with FILE_IN_USE. (b) rename(tmp -> app.asar) fails permanently and rename(_app.asar -> app.asar) fails once: patchInstall still returns a rolled-back FILE_IN_USE and Discord's original is back at app.asar. Fails today with ROLLBACK_FAILED. (c) fixture with app.asar absent, _app.asar original, .subline-app.asar.tmp present: patchInstall returns ok, backupCreated false, verifyPatch passes. Fails today with BROKEN_INSTALL. Flow test: inspect returns broken/asar-missing-backup-present -> state.actions contains 'repair'; sending it calls unpatch once and the next inspect is unpatched.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in direction. Adjust it in four places. (1) Keep the shared renameWithRetry, but put it in the patcher package backed by realFs (modInstall.ts can keep node:fs because the bundle dir is not an asar path; tests/realFs.test.ts forbids node:fs inside patcher/, so the shared helper must import from ./realFs.js). Use it for all three renames in applyPatch/rollback AND for the restore rename in restoreOriginal (patch.ts:687), since uninstall on Windows has the same AV exposure and the product rule says uninstall must always work. Also retry unlinkSync in discard() for the same errnos, or a stranded tmp held by AV is fine but should be logged, not silent. (2) Do not teach patchInstall to "finish" an interrupted patch by renaming a freshly staged stub onto app.asar. The simpler and already-verified path is restore-then-patch: when inspectInstall reports broken/asar-missing-backup-present and readIsOriginalAsar(backupPath) is true, patchInstall first calls the same code as restoreOriginal (renameWithRetry(_app.asar -> app.asar), remove marker, verify original), re-inspects, and then runs the normal unpatched path. This reuses restoreOriginal's corruption checks, leaves backupCreated true (one code path, one report shape), and never trusts a stale .subline-app.asar.tmp from a previous run. Make the helper's decideRepatch depend on this so an asar-missing-backup-present install owned by Subline is repaired on the next helper run instead of looping on BROKEN_INSTALL. (3) In the flow, broken-install for reasons asar-missing-backup-present and our-patch-without-backup must offer a "repair" action that calls ports.unpatch and then inspectChosen again; the ROLLBACK_FAILED and BROKEN_INSTALL copy should name that button, not a manual file move. (4) For the FILE_IN_USE copy: in flow.failPatch, when the error code is FILE_IN_USE and ports.listProcesses shows no Discord process for the branch, replace the message with "Another program (often antivirus) is still scanning Discord's files. Wait a few seconds and try again." rather than hardcoding that into fsError, which is also used by uninstall where Discord may genuinely be open. Tests: add a rename seam to PatchHooks (hooks.rename, defaulting to realFs renameSync, with sleepSync like modInstall) and cover: EPERM once on tmp->app.asar then success (win32) returns ok; EPERM permanent on tmp->app.asar plus EPERM once on _app.asar->app.asar returns FILE_IN_USE with the original back at app.asar; same on darwin is not retried; fixture with app.asar absent and _app.asar original returns ok via restore-then-patch; a fixture where _app.asar is a stub returns BACKUP_CORRUPT and touches nothing; flow test that broken/asar-missing-backup-present yields actions containing "repair", the action calls unpatch once, and the next inspect is unpatched; helper test that the same state is repaired on a run instead of logging a failed repatch.

title: Fresh install from the DMG or a translocated copy registers a LaunchAgent pointing at a path that vanishes; helper never runs again, done screen says background updates are on
scenario: User opens Subline.dmg and double-clicks Subline.app inside the mounted image (appPath /Volumes/Subline/Subline.app), or runs a quarantined Subline.app from ~/Downloads (Gatekeeper translocates it to /private/var/folders/.../AppTranslocation/<uuid>/d/Subline.app). Fresh install runs to completion: patch ok -> installHelper -> installHelperFor -> installLaunchAgent -> bootstrap -> isLoaded true -> done screen. User ejects the DMG or the translocation mount disappears at quit. Discord updates a week later.
whatHappens: installHelperFor (lines 171-197) has no check on wiring.appPath; helperWiring() in main.ts line 420 derives it from app.getPath("exe"), so the plist ProgramArguments names the /Volumes or AppTranslocation path. launchd loads it for this session (isLoaded true, so HelperInstallOutcome.installed = true and the done screen carries 'Updates are handled in the background'). After the volume is gone every launchd start fails (no such file); RunAtLoad at next login fails too. The guard exists only in ensureHelperFor (line 297) and ensureHelperFromHelper (line 379), which never run on the fresh-install path. The next Discord update wipes the patch and nothing repairs it: Subline silently stops working, violating 'Subline must survive Discord self-updates'. Nothing in main.ts calls app.moveToApplicationsFolder or warns before Welcome.
fix: Two layers. (1) In installHelperFor (darwin) refuse when appPath starts with /Volumes/ or contains /AppTranslocation/: return HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED with copy 'Subline is running from the disk image. Drag Subline to Applications, open it from there, and press Try again.' The existing helper-failed screen offers retry and skip-helper; skip must keep saying what it costs. (2) Earlier and better: in flow.start() or detect(), a port isRunningFromTemporaryLocation(); when true show a new step 'move-to-applications' before anything is written (actions: recheck, cancel), so the TCC grant and the helper both attach to the permanent copy. ensureHelperFor already has the predicate; export it and reuse it in both places.
test: tests/helperWiring.test.ts: installHelperFor({appPath: "/Volumes/Subline/Subline.app", ...fakeLaunchctl}, "darwin", home) returns ok:false with code HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED and fakeLaunchctl.bootstrap was never called; same for "/private/var/folders/ab/T/AppTranslocation/1234/d/Subline.app". Flow test: with ports reporting a temporary location, the flow never reaches 'patching' and patchCalls is empty. Both fail today (bootstrap is called, outcome installed:true).
betterFix: The proposed two layers are right, with three corrections. (1) The helper-failed copy must not say "press Try again": retry calls ports.installHelper in the same process, whose appPath is still the /Volumes or translocated path, so it fails identically. Say instead: "Subline is running from the disk image. Quit Subline, drag it to Applications, and open it from there. It finishes the setup on its own." That second run lands on already-installed and ensureHelperFor registers the agent with reason "missing", which is the recovery path and should be asserted in a flow test. (2) Put the predicate in one exported function, e.g. isTemporaryAppLocation(appPath) in installer/src/helper/launchAgent.ts (startsWith "/Volumes/" or includes "/AppTranslocation/"), and use it in installHelperFor (refuse with HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED, also covering the helper:install IPC at main.ts:453), ensureHelperFor, ensureHelperFromHelper, and a new FlowPorts.runningFromTemporaryLocation() checked in flow.start()/detect() before any write, before the Discord-closed gate and before the App Management prompt. (3) Fix the neighbour: flow.ts ensureHelper() must return false when result.value.action is "skipped" with reason "running-from-temporary-location", and the already-installed copy must then say to move the app, not "Updates are handled in the background". Prefer a real action over instructions: the move-to-applications step should offer a "Move to Applications" action backed by a port that calls Electron's app.moveToApplicationsFolder() in main.ts (it moves the bundle and relaunches from /Applications; it works from both a DMG and a translocated copy), with "cancel" as the other action; keep the recheck for the case the user moved it by hand. Tests: helperWiring.test.ts, installHelperFor with both temporary paths returns ok:false, code HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED, no bootstrap call, no plist written; flow.test.ts, ports reporting a temporary location never reaches "patching" (patchCalls empty) and the step is "move-to-applications"; already-installed with a temporary location reports helperOk false; ensureHelperFromHelper keeps returning "skipped" (the helper must never fail a repair run over this). All fail today. Windows is unaffected: NSIS installs to a fixed path and executablePath is the installed exe.

title: Marker loss root cause: Vencord's persistAfterDiscordUpdates ships in patcher.js and copies the stub, never the marker; after the classify fix both app and helper still misbehave on the marker-less install
scenario: 1. Subline patches app-1.0.9258 (stub + _app.asar + subline-patch.json). 2. Discord downloads 9259 while running; the helper sees 9259 unpatched and defers for as long as Discord sits in the tray (log 2026-09-24 19:06 to 09-25 16:11, need=injection-wiped settle=discord-running). 3. The user quits Discord. Vencord's `persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts` (pinned commit 7f0c10cc, compiled into build/mod/patcher.js, nothing in scripts/buildMod.mjs removes it and DISABLE_UPDATER_AUTO_PATCHING is never set) runs on before-quit: renameSync(9259/app.asar -> _app.asar); copyFileSync(9258/app.asar -> 9259/app.asar). It never copies subline-patch.json. 4. Next helper run (log 2026-10-04 12:01): stub loads Subline's own patcher.js, _app.asar is the original, marker absent -> classifyStub -> patched-by-other 'another client mod' -> abandoned. Same again for 9260 on 10-05. 5. User opens Subline -> mod-conflict -> Uninstall -> FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (log 10-06 12:08:07). 6. NOW ASSUME the classify fix lands (stub loading our loader = ours, marker null). To turn Subline back on, right-click ... Quit Discord' (helper.ts:704). whatHappens: The marker is lost on every Windows Discord update that happens while Discord is open (the common case), by code Subline ships. Add `adoptInstall(install, bundle, productVersion)` in patcher/patch.ts: when the stub already loads bundle.loaderPath and _app.asar reads as original, write (or refresh) subline-patch.json from readDiscordVersion and bundle.buildId and verify; no asar rename, so it works with Discord running on Windows. In decideRepatch, return a new reason `marker-stale` when the stub's loaderPath === bundle.loaderPath and only the marker is missing or names another build; reconcile handles marker-stale with adoptInstall before awaitDiscordSettled (never deferred, never alerts). In flow.alreadyInstalled, decide 'update' from the installed bundle itself: inspectModBundle(dirname(installState.loaderPath)) buildId vs shipped, not from the marker; and call adoptInstall on that path so the app also rewrites the marker. Same with a marker naming an older build id -> marker rewritten, no quit-required after 31 min and a second run. flow.test: inspect returns patched-by-us with marker null and shipped buildId !== installed bundle manifest -> 'flow.update-detected' and patchCalls=1; with the same build -> already-installed and the marker file exists afterwards. Each fails on main.

In patcher/patch.ts needsMarkerRewrite (or adoptPatch's own check): also true when state.kind is patched-by-us, the stub's loaderPath equals bundle.loaderPath (compare with sameLoaderPath, not ===), the backup is original, and marker.pluginBuildId !== bundle.buildId. adoptPatch then rewrites the marker with bundle.buildId and reports warning "marker-stale". In helper decideRepatch, return marker-missing (or a new marker-stale) for that case before verifyPatch, so reconcile adopts without awaitDiscordSettled. Do not make it silent: after a build-id adoption while Discord runs, raise the existing restart-required "Subline updated. Quit and reopen Discord to use the new version." (same key as today), because the running Discord still has the old patcher loaded. Never raise quit-required for it. title: Helper's mtimeOf uses Electron-patched node:fs on app.asar; every Windows helper repatch fails FILE_IN_USE and the settle quiet window reads fake mtimes
scenario: Fresh install succeeds. Discord self-updates (new app-1.0.x folder on Windows, app.asar replaced on macOS). The helper runs: collectManaged -> reconcile -> awaitDiscordSettled -> sample() -> ports.mtimeOf(install.asarPath) and mtimeOf(install.backupPath). Then ports.patch -> patchInstall -> renameSync(asarPath, backupPath).
whatHappens: helper/ports.ts line 12 imports statSync from "node:fs" and line 387 calls statSync(path).mtimeMs on install.asarPath and install.backupPath (settle.ts watchedPaths, line 134). Inside the packaged helper (Electron, isHelperRun) node:fs is the asar-hooked module: a stat on a path ending in .asar goes through getOrCreateArchive, which opens the archive and caches its file handle for the process lifetime. realFs.ts (lines 17-26) and tests/realFs.test.ts document exactly this failure: on Windows the handle has no FILE_SHARE_DELETE, so the later renameSync(app.asar, _app.asar) in patch.ts line 243 fails with a sharing violation (EBUSY/EPERM -> FILE_IN_USE). Second effect on both OSes: Electron's asar stat returns a fake mtime (process start time) for app.asar/_app.asar, so the quiet-window check in settle.ts lines 216-219 measures time since the helper started, not file activity; it 'settles' after ~13 s even mid-update. The owner's Windows log never shows a completed helper repatch (every attempt was deferred while Discord ran), so this is latent and unverified in the field, but it is the same mechanism realFs.ts calls 'a real shipped failure'. tests/realFs.test.ts line 46 lists only app/uninstall.ts outside patcher/, so nothing guards helper/ports.ts.
fix: In helper/ports.ts import statSync from "../patcher/realFs.js" for mtimeOf (keep node:fs only for the non-asar calls, or add statSync to realFs exports which already has it). Add "helper/ports.ts" to ASAR_TOUCHING_OUTSIDE_PATCHER in tests/realFs.test.ts so the import list is enforced.
test: tests/realFs.test.ts: add "helper/ports.ts" to ASAR_TOUCHING_OUTSIDE_PATCHER. The existing per-file assertion (no asar-sensitive names imported from node:fs, and the source contains "realFs.js") fails on current code because statSync comes from node:fs and realFs.js is not imported. Additionally a settle unit test: mtimeOf returning a constant equal to now() for the asar paths and a real old mtime for resourcesPath must still require quietMs of genuine quiet; it documents why fake times are unacceptable.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right but incomplete. 1) In installer/src/helper/ports.ts import statSync from "../patcher/realFs.js" for ALL its uses, not only mtimeOf: the realFs test asserts on imported names, so leaving the findBundleRoot statSync calls (lines 145-159) on node:fs would still fail the guard. 2) Invert the guard in tests/realFs.test.ts so it cannot be forgotten again: enumerate every file under src/ that imports an ASAR_SENSITIVE name from node:fs and require it to be on an explicit allowlist of files that never see a Discord path (app/log.ts, app/language.ts, app/patchedInstalls.ts, helper/state.ts, helper/alerts.ts, helper/launchAgent.ts, helper/scheduledTask.ts, main/main.ts, main/ports.ts, bundle/spec.ts, bundle/bundle.ts, verify/beacon.ts, app/modInstall.ts, app/appManagement.ts). A new file that imports statSync or existsSync from node:fs then fails until someone states it never touches an asar. The hand list ASAR_TOUCHING_OUTSIDE_PATCHER missed helper/ports.ts exactly as it once missed locate.ts. 3) Add a settle unit test: mtimeOf returns a constant equal to ports.now() at start for the two asar paths and an old real mtime for the others; the current code must require quietMs of genuine quiet, which documents that a fake constant mtime delays every run and masks in-place asar writes. 4) Optional hardening: have the helper log a warning once if usingOriginalFs is false inside an Electron run (process.versions.electron set), since the header already records originalFs and a false value there is the only field signal of this class of bug.

title: DiagnosticsLog.append throws on ENOSPC or an unwritable log dir, which throws out of every flow transition and freezes the installer on a busy screen
scenario: Disk is full (or ~/Library/Logs/Subline / %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline\logs is not writable, e.g. created by another account or an elevated run). User presses Continue on any screen; the flow calls this.set(), which calls ports.log.info (flow.ts line 486).
whatHappens: append() (lines 212-216) does mkdirSync, rotateIfNeeded and appendFileSync with no try/catch, so log.info throws. dispatch() has no catch, the ipcMain.handle promise rejects, and the renderer's act() (renderer.ts line 548: render(await api.send(action))) never calls render. The window stays on the last painted state, typically a busy screen with no buttons, and the footer Uninstall is disabled while busy with no actions (renderer line 166). On a full disk this is the exact moment the user needs the ENOSPC message that patchInstall would have produced. The flow's own state machine never reaches the patch at all.
fix: Make DiagnosticsLog never throw: wrap append (and writeHeader, copyBundle's read) in try/catch, remember the last failure (errno and path) in a field, write it to stderr once, and expose it in the diagnostics header so the next successful write records that lines were lost. Separately, in main.ts wrap the flow:send/flow:start handlers so a thrown error becomes a FlowState of step patch-failed (or a generic 'failed') with the cause, so the screen always has a button.
test: tests/log.test.ts: construct DiagnosticsLog with dir set to the path of an existing regular file (mkdir fails with ENOTDIR/EEXIST); info('x') does not throw and lastWriteError names the errno. Fails today with a thrown error. Flow test: a logger whose info throws once during set(): send() still resolves to a state with at least one action.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right but incomplete. Do all of this: (1) In log.ts, make append, writeHeader and rotateIfNeeded never throw. Catch every fs error, store {code, path, count} in a `lastWriteError` field, write one line to process.stderr the first time, and have the next successful append prepend a `subline.log.lost` entry with the count and errno. Make copyBundle and read tolerate an unreadable rotated file (readFileSync inside try/catch; existsSync is not enough for EACCES). Keep the redaction path unchanged. (2) In main.ts, the startup path must not depend on the log: move createWindow() ahead of the header write, or keep the order and rely on the never-throw log; and the uncaughtException and unhandledRejection handlers must stay safe once the log cannot throw. (3) Wrap flow:start, flow:send and flow:restart handlers in try/catch that returns a FlowState with step "failed", the cause as a named error (code from errno when present), and actions ["copy-diagnostics", "finish"] or whatever terminal action set the renderer already renders, so every screen keeps a button. (4) In renderer.ts act(), catch a rejected api.send and render a failed state with a way out, as defence in depth for any other throw. (5) Tests that fail today: log.test.ts: dir is an existing regular file; info("x") does not throw, lastWriteError.code is EEXIST or ENOTDIR. log.test.ts: a dir that becomes unwritable after the header, then writable again; the next line records the lost count. flow.test.ts: a logger that throws once inside set(); send() resolves to a state with actions.length > 0. A main-level test (or the existing helperWiring/ports harness) that the flow:send handler returns a state with actions when the flow throws.

title: Hand-picking the Discord branch folder on Windows is refused as 'not a Discord installation'
scenario: Discord is installed somewhere unusual (custom LOCALAPPDATA, second drive, or LOCALAPPDATA unset so defaultSearchRoots is empty). The not-found screen says 'choose it by hand'. The folder picker (openDirectory only) opens and the user picks the obvious folder, D:\Apps\Discord, which holds Update.exe and app-1.0.9260.
whatHappens: describeExplicitPath (lines 250-270) builds the install straight from rootPath, so resourcesPath is D:\Apps\Discord\resources, which does not exist, and it returns NOT_A_DISCORD_INSTALL 'does not look like a Discord installation (no app.asar under …\Discord\resources)'. locateDiscordInstalls then fails the whole call (line 206). The user is back on discord-not-found with no hint that they must open the hidden app-1.0.xxxx subfolder; most users give up here. The same user on the uninstall side is fine because uninstallTargets sweeps app-* under a remembered stableId, but a remembered entry only exists after a successful patch.
fix: In describeExplicitPath on win32: if rootPath itself does not look like Discord but contains app-<version> children, use findWindowsAppDirs(rootPath) and take the newest that looksLikeDiscord (stableId becomes rootPath, which stableIdFor already yields). Keep the explicit flag true. Improve the refusal copy to name the expected layout when no child matches.
test: tests/locate.test.ts: temp dir Discord/ with app-1.0.1/resources/app.asar and app-1.0.2/resources/app.asar; locateDiscordInstalls({platform:'win32', explicitPaths:[Discord], searchRoots: []}) returns one install whose rootPath is app-1.0.2 and stableId is Discord. Fails today with NOT_A_DISCORD_INSTALL.
betterFix: The proposed fix is correct and sufficient for the stated scenario. Two neighbours should be closed in the same change. 1) In describeExplicitPath on win32, after the direct check fails, call findWindowsAppDirs(rootPath) and take the first child where looksLikeDiscord is true (newest first, same rule as the search path); keep fromExplicitPath true; branch comes from branchFromPath(rootPath) which already matches 'discord' in the parent path, so stableIdFor(child) returns rootPath as the finding says. 2) Also accept a pick of the resources folder itself on either OS: if basename(rootPath) is 'resources' (win32) or the path ends in Contents/Resources (darwin) and its parent looks like Discord, climb to the parent. 3) Refusal copy must name the expected layout in plain words, for example 'Pick the Discord folder, usually C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Discord, or the app-1.0.xxxx folder inside it', instead of the internal 'no app.asar under ...\resources'. Keep the error out of locateDiscordInstalls' fail-the-whole-call behaviour as is, since an explicit bad pick should still show the not-found screen. Tests (tests/locate.test.ts): a) the finding's test, which fails today; b) the same tree with only app-1.0.2 holding app.asar and app-1.0.1 empty, expect rootPath app-1.0.2; c) a branch folder whose app-* children have no asar at all, expect NOT_A_DISCORD_INSTALL and a message that mentions 'app-1.0'; d) an explicit pick of Discord/app-1.0.2/resources, expect rootPath app-1.0.2. Also add a flow.test.ts case that after this located install is patched, patchedInstalls remembers stableId = Discord so uninstallTargets sweeps the next app-* after a Discord update.

title: Helper only adopts an install it has already seen itself; the installer never seeds helper-state.json and collectManaged ignores patched-installs.json, so an update before the helper's first observation orphans a fresh install
scenario: Fresh install completes: patch ok, rememberPatchedInstall writes patched-installs.json, installHelper registers the task/agent. Before the helper's first run observes the install as patched-by-us (up to 5 min on Windows; also any time helper-state.json is missing, corrupt, or deleted by a keepSettings=false uninstall followed by a reinstall), Discord updates: new app-1.0.x folder on Windows, or app.asar replaced on macOS. Helper runs.
whatHappens: collectManaged line 448: remembered = run.state.installs[install.stableId] where run.state comes only from helper-state.json, which only the helper writes (rememberInstall, runHelperOnce writeState). The flow writes patched-installs.json instead, which the helper's locate() merges (helper/ports.ts 347) but collectManaged never consults. oursNow is false (unpatched after the update) and oursOnce is false (no memory), so line 452 logs not-ours and the install is abandoned permanently with summary 'Subline is not installed in any Discord that could be found'. This is the exact pattern in the owner's log from 2026-09-03 17:47 onward (app-1.0.9256 not-ours for days). The product rule 'the helper must never abandon an install it owns' is broken by a race nobody can see.
fix: Two parts. (1) At install time the flow seeds the helper memory: a FlowPorts.rememberForHelper(install, buildId, discordVersion) port that reads helper-state.json, sets installs[stableId] = {discordVersion, buildId, patchedAt: now, failures: 0}, and writes it atomically (writeHelperState). (2) collectManaged treats every stableId in patched-installs.json as oursOnce as well (ports.readState can merge it, or a ports.rememberedStableIds() port). Also log the stableId on not-ours so the next log reader can see what the helper compared.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: helper state empty, patched-installs.json (or the new port) lists the install's stableId, install inspects as unpatched with _app.asar absent, bundle valid, Discord closed: runHelperOnce repatches it (report.repatched has the path). Fails today with decisions containing not-ours. Flow test: after a successful patch the fake rememberForHelper port was called with the install's stableId and the patch report's build id.
betterFix: Do part (2) only; drop part (1). Part (1) makes the flow a second writer of helper-state.json, and a helper run already in progress (Windows runs can wait minutes for Discord to close; it reads state at start and writes at end) clobbers the seed, reopening the same window. patched-installs.json is written atomically by the flow alone and read fresh by every helper run, so it is the right source. Concretely: add HelperPorts.rememberedStableIds(): string[] (ports.ts: readPatchedInstalls(productDir).map(e => e.stableId), already imported there), and in collectManaged set oursOnce = remembered !== undefined || run.ports.rememberedStableIds?.().includes(install.stableId). Keep the patched-by-other and other-account checks after it so a foreign mod or another account is still never touched. Log stableId on the not-ours decision. After the repair, rememberInstall writes helper state as today. Tests: helper.test.ts with the harness port returning [fixture.install.stableId], empty helper state, install unpatched after simulateDiscordUpdate, Discord closed: expect report.repatched to contain the rootPath and no "helper.scan not-ours"; fails today. Also a port test that createHelperPorts reads the ids from patched-installs.json. Keep the existing "never patched" test (port returns []) so a truly foreign Discord stays untouched.

title: chosenInstall is frozen at detect time; on Windows a Discord update during the activation or permission wait makes the patch land in a folder Discord no longer runs
scenario: Fresh install on Windows. detect() picks app-1.0.9258 (newest). User reaches 'Finish paying in your browser' (poll up to 48 h, line 1401) or 'Turn on Subline' (no timeout) or leaves 'Discord is running' open. Meanwhile Discord's Squirrel updater lays down app-1.0.9259 beside it (it does this while Discord runs, before any restart). Payment lands -> activated -> checkRunning -> quit -> permissionStep -> applyPatch.
whatHappens: applyPatch (line 1736) uses this.chosenInstall, never re-locating. installModBundle + patch write into app-1.0.9258. launchDiscord (main/ports.ts line 576) spawns app-1.0.9258\Discord.exe directly, so the beacon confirms and the done screen shows a green tick. Every later launch from the Start Menu goes through Update.exe into app-1.0.9259, which has no Subline: silent failure right after a confirmed install. The helper's first run (within 5 min) locates the newest folder (9259), finds it unpatched, has no helper-state memory for the stableId (see the next finding) and logs not-ours forever. patched-installs.json names 9258 but locateRemembered resolves it to the newest folder anyway. Vencord's own persistAfterDiscordUpdates only runs on before-quit of a Discord that loaded Subline, which 9259 never does.
fix: In applyPatch (and stageUpdate), before installModBundle: re-run ports.locate(explicitPaths) and, on win32, replace chosenInstall with the newest located install whose stableId equals chosenInstall.stableId; re-inspect it and, if it is not unpatched/ours, route through inspectChosen again. Log 'patch.target-moved' with from/to. Also launch through the branch folder's Discord.exe launcher (…\Discord\Discord.exe, which is Update.exe's stub and always runs the newest folder) instead of the versioned exe, so what the user sees after install is what they will see tomorrow.
test: tests/flow.test.ts: locate returns [app-1.0.1] during detect and [app-1.0.2] (same stableId) when called again after activation; drive the flow to patching and assert patchCalls[0].install.rootPath ends with app-1.0.2 and launchDiscord was called with it. Fails today (patch called with app-1.0.1).
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in direction but needs four corrections. 1) Place the re-locate in applyPatch AFTER the listProcesses check (Discord is closed there, so Squirrel cannot move the folder between re-locate and patch); stageUpdate needs no re-locate because it writes no patch. Also wait for no `Update.exe` process after the quit, because a forced quit can land mid-extraction and leave a half-written app folder that already passes looksLikeDiscord (resources/app.asar exists). 2) Re-locate via `ports.locate(explicitPaths)` and pick the install whose stableId equals chosenInstall.stableId; if none is found, do not patch the stale folder: fail with a named error (e.g. DISCORD_MOVED) that says Discord changed under the installer and offers retry. Re-inspect the new folder; continue only when kind is `unpatched` or `patched-by-us`; anything else goes back through inspectChosen. Log `patch.target-moved` with from/to. Apply on every platform, not only win32 (cheap, and it covers a hand-picked path that vanished). 3) Do not launch `…\Discord\Discord.exe`: that root stub is a Squirrel StubExecutable feature and I could not confirm Discord ships it. Discord's Start Menu shortcut target is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Discord\Update.exe --processStart Discord.exe`. Launch that when `join(install.stableId, "Update.exe")` exists, else fall back to the versioned exe. Verify the path on the Windows box before relying on it; this Mac cannot. 4) Close the helper side too, or the same install still dies silently when the race is missed: the helper must treat an install listed in patched-installs.json (matched by stableId) as owned, not only state.installs[stableId], and the installer should seed helper-state.json for the patched stableId. Test changes: installer/tests/flow.test.ts `script.installs` is a static Result (line 117); make it accept a function or an array of answers per call, then assert patchCalls[0] targets app-1.0.2, rememberPatchedInstall got app-1.0.2, and launchDiscord was called with app-1.0.2 (plus a case where the second locate returns nothing and the flow lands on a named failure, not a patch). Both fail today.

title: installHelperFor registers a LaunchAgent that points at the DMG or the translocated copy, so the helper dies after its first run
scenario: 1. User opens Subline.dmg and double-clicks Subline.app inside it (or runs a quarantined copy that Gatekeeper translocates to /private/var/folders/.../AppTranslocation/...). 2. Install succeeds; flow.ts:1838 calls installHelperFor, which writes a plist whose ProgramArguments[0] is /Volumes/Subline/Subline.app/Contents/MacOS/Subline (or the translocation path). 3. launchctl bootstrap succeeds and RunAtLoad runs the helper once while the mount still exists, so the screen says updates are handled in the background. 4. The user ejects the DMG. Every later StartInterval, WatchPaths and login start fails with a missing executable; launchd logs it, Subline never does.
whatHappens: Self-repair is silently dead for everyone who installs without first dragging the app to Applications, which is the common path. The next Discord update wipes the stub and nothing repairs it; no alert is possible because the helper cannot start. ensureHelperFor (ports.ts:297) already refuses these paths with running-from-temporary-location, and the test at tests/helperWiring.test.ts:560 covers only that function; installHelperFor has no guard and no test.
fix: In installHelperFor (and installLaunchAgent) refuse an appPath that starts with /Volumes/ or contains /AppTranslocation/ with a named error such as HELPER_APP_LOCATION_TEMPORARY. In the flow, detect this before patching: on macOS when app.getPath('exe') is under /Volumes or AppTranslocation, show a screen that says 'Move Subline to your Applications folder first' and offer Electron's app.moveToApplicationsFolder(); fall back to the helper-failed screen whose copy says the same. Also handle a later move of Subline.app: the already-installed path repairs it today (ensureHelperFor points-elsewhere), so add the same check to the done screen copy: 'Keep Subline in Applications so it can keep repairing Discord.'
test: tests/helperWiring.test.ts: installHelperFor({...wiring(), appPath: '/Volumes/Subline/Subline.app'}, 'darwin', home) returns an error and writes no plist; same for a path containing /AppTranslocation/. tests/flow.test.ts: a flow whose helper wiring reports the temporary location stops on the move-to-applications screen before patch is called. Both fail on main.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in shape; three refinements. 1. One shared predicate (e.g. temporaryAppLocation(appPath) in helper/launchAgent.ts) used by installHelperFor, ensureHelperFor, ensureHelperFromHelper and the flow, instead of the string checks duplicated at ports.ts:298 and :380. 2. A bare "/Volumes/" prefix refusal also blocks a Subline kept on an external or second internal disk, which is a stable location. Keep "/AppTranslocation/" as a hard refusal, and for "/Volumes/" confirm the mount is a disk image (hdiutil info -plist, match the mount-point prefix) before refusing; if hdiutil cannot be read, fall back to the prefix heuristic and refuse, since a dead helper is the worse outcome. 3. Put the check before patching as a FlowPorts port (e.g. appLocation(): Result<{stable: boolean; path: string}>) so flow.test.ts can drive it without touching Electron; the screen offers app.moveToApplicationsFolder() and a cancel, and the retry on helper-failed re-runs the same check so it cannot loop. Also make flow.ts ensureHelper() treat action "skipped" with reason "running-from-temporary-location" as not ok, so the already-installed copy stops claiming background updates work. Tests: installHelperFor with a /Volumes/<dmg> or /AppTranslocation/ appPath returns HELPER_APP_LOCATION_TEMPORARY and writes no plist; installHelperFor with /Volumes/ExternalDisk/Subline.app and an hdiutil port that lists no such image succeeds; flow stops on the move-to-applications screen before patch is called; already-installed screen says the helper is off when ensureHelper skips. All fail on main.

title: discardUnpacked deletes the user's whole temp directory when a release zip has the bundle at its root
scenario: 1. unpackArchive writes the zip to <tmpdir>/subline-update-XXXX/ and extracts to <tmpdir>/subline-update-XXXX/unpacked. 2. findBundleRoot(target) returns target itself when subline-mod.json is at the archive root (ports.ts:145), a layout it explicitly supports. 3. downloadAndInstall's finally calls discardUnpacked(found) which runs rmSync(join(found, '..', '..'), {recursive: true, force: true}). With found = .../unpacked that resolves to os.tmpdir(): /var/folders/xx/yy/T on macOS, %TEMP% on Windows. 4. The only thing preventing this today is the --keepParent flag in scripts/release.mjs:265; a hand-built or future release zip without the wrapper folder triggers it on every machine at the next 6 hour check.
whatHappens: The helper recursively force-deletes the per-user temp directory in the background, taking other applications' sockets, caches and in-progress downloads with it. There is no test for discardUnpacked and no guard on the path.
fix: Have unpack return both the bundle dir and the scratch root ({bundleDir, scratchDir}) and have discardUnpacked remove scratchDir only. Add a guard that refuses to delete any path whose basename does not start with 'subline-update-'. Keep findBundleRoot as is.
test: tests/ports.test.ts: call unpackArchive with a fake exec that writes subline-mod.json and patcher.js directly into the target (root layout), then discardUnpacked on the result; assert the scratch directory is gone and a sentinel file created beside it in the same tmpdir still exists. Fails on main (sentinel deleted).
betterFix: The proposed fix is correct. Two refinements. 1. Keep the port signature as is and add a pure helper `scratchRootOf(bundleDir)` in ports.ts that walks up from bundleDir until the basename starts with "subline-update-" and the parent is tmpdir(); it returns null otherwise. discardUnpacked removes only that root and does nothing on null. This avoids touching helper.ts and the HelperPorts type in helper.ts:109-110 while an implementer is concurrently editing the branch, and the guard is unit-testable without a real archive. Returning {bundleDir, scratchDir} is also fine if the Fix phase prefers it; do not pass "..".."" arithmetic anywhere. 2. Add two tests. tests/ports.test.ts: unpackArchive with a fake exec that writes subline-mod.json plus the renderer into the target root, then discardUnpacked; assert the scratch dir is gone and a sentinel file beside it in tmpdir survives (fails on current code). Also a wrapped-layout case asserting the scratch dir is removed. tests/release.test.ts: assert the mod archive ditto call includes --keepParent, so the release layout cannot drift without a red test.

title: A helper killed between the two renames leaves Discord with no app.asar, and nothing automatic repairs it
scenario: 1. The helper is in applyPatch: step 2 renameSync(app.asar -> _app.asar) done, step 3 renameSync(tmp -> app.asar) not yet. 2.
