It is killed: macOS logout or shutdown sends SIGTERM to the agent, uninstall's launchctl bootout (launchAgent.ts:295) kills a running job, Windows uninstall runs schtasks /End (scheduledTask.ts:354), Task Scheduler enforces ExecutionTimeLimit PT10M (scheduledTask.ts:157) and two installs mid-update can exceed it, or power is lost. 3. Resources now holds _app.asar and .subline-app.asar.tmp and no app.asar. Discord does not start. 4. Next helper run: inspectInstall says broken (asar-missing-backup-present, state.ts:162, which the type comment calls Recoverable). decideRepatch returns broken-install, patchInstall refuses with BROKEN_INSTALL at guardPatchable, handlePatchFailure finds BROKEN_INSTALL in IMMEDIATE_PATCH_ALERTS and notifies 'Discord updated and Subline could not put its translation back. Discord itself is fine. Open Subline to finish.' 5. The user opens Subline: flow.ts:795 shows broken-install with Retry and Cancel only; Retry re-detects the same state. Only Uninstall (unpatchBroken -> restoreOriginal) fixes it.
whatHappens: Discord cannot start, the helper says Discord is fine, and the app offers no repair. The window is milliseconds but the consequence breaks the product rule that Discord must always start, and the recovery gap is permanent until the user finds Uninstall.
fix: Make the interrupted patch finishable. In patchInstall, when state.kind is broken with reason asar-missing-backup-present: discard the temp file, renameSync(_app.asar -> app.asar), re-inspect, and continue as unpatched (or, equivalently, write the stub straight to app.asar since _app.asar is the verified original, then verify). In the helper keep broken-install as a reason but let it reach that path. In flow.ts give broken-install a Repair action for that reason that calls the same code. Keep the alert text honest: for broken reasons say 'Discord may not start until this is repaired' instead of 'Discord itself is fine'.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: patchForReal, run, then unlink app.asar and write .subline-app.asar.tmp to mimic the kill; run again and expect repatched to contain the install, inspectInstall kind patched-by-us, _app.asar still the original bytes, and no repatch-failed notification. tests/patch.test.ts: patchInstall on a fixture made with withoutAsar and withBackup returns ok with backupCreated false. Both fail on main (BROKEN_INSTALL).
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in direction but incomplete in three places. 1. Guard the backup before finishing. asar-missing-backup-present only says app.asar is absent and _app.asar exists. _app.asar can be a stale foreign stub. Finish the interrupted patch only when readIsOriginalAsar(_app.asar) is ok and true (the same check restoreOriginal uses at patch.ts:670). Otherwise keep BROKEN_INSTALL with a backup-corrupt message. 2. Restore first, then patch normally. In patchInstall, for that reason: discard .subline-app.asar.tmp, renameSync(_app.asar -> app.asar), re-inspect, then fall through to applyPatch as unpatched. This beats writing the stub straight onto app.asar because if the following patch fails, rollback leaves a Discord that starts. Share the restore code with restoreOriginal rather than a second copy. 3. Use the startable value the helper already computes. handlePatchFailure has startable (helper.ts:797) but ignores it for the alert text. When startable is false and the reason is not in BACKUP_GONE_REASONS, say 'Discord may not start until this is repaired. Open Subline and choose Repair.' Keep 'Discord itself is fine' only when startable is true. Also flip the existing test at tests/patch.test.ts:367; it asserts BROKEN_INSTALL for this fixture and will fail once the fix lands. For flow.ts, the simplest safe route is: for broken with reason asar-missing-backup-present, do not stop at the broken-install screen; route into the normal install path, since patchInstall now repairs it and Discord cannot be running without app.asar. That also covers the GUI installer killed in the same window, which has no helper memory. Add a state.test.ts case for asar-missing-backup-present with a stub in _app.asar to prove the guard in point 1 refuses it.

title: Uninstall's helper-stop failure tells Windows users to restart their Mac
scenario: 1. On Windows removeScheduledTask fails (schtasks /Delete refused, or the task still lists after deletion, scheduledTask.ts:356-366). 2. removeHelperFor returns error, uninstall() refuses at step 0 and returns the summary 'Subline could not stop its background updater, so nothing was removed ... restart your Mac and try again.'
whatHappens: The only remedy offered is wrong for the platform, so a Windows user who hits a Task Scheduler refusal has no usable next step and Subline cannot be removed.
fix: Pass the platform (or a helper-removal remedy string) into uninstall() and render 'restart your computer and try again, or delete the task \Subline\Helper in Task Scheduler' on win32 and 'restart your Mac' on darwin.
test: tests/uninstall.test.ts: with platform win32 and helper {applicable: true, removed: false, error: HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED}, the summary mentions Task Scheduler and not 'Mac'. Fails on main.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in substance; put the platform on UninstallPorts rather than UninstallOptions. uninstall() does no I/O by design and every environment fact already arrives through ports (modBundleDir, productDir, logDir); tests build ports once via ports(), so one place changes. In uninstall.ts add `platform: NodeJS.Platform` to UninstallPorts, and in the step-0 refusal pick the remedy by platform: win32: "restart your computer and try again. If it still fails, open Task Scheduler, find the task Subline\Helper, and delete it, then run Uninstall again." darwin: "restart your Mac and try again." Pass `platform: process.platform` from installer/src/main/main.ts:659 (next to ...uninstallPaths()). Tests in installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: (1) platform win32 + helper {applicable: true, removed: false, error: HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED}: summary contains "Task Scheduler" and does not contain "Mac"; (2) platform darwin: summary contains "Mac" and not "Task Scheduler". Both fail on the current code. Optional neighbour to cover while there: the same HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED code is used for "schtasks refused" and "task still listed", so the summary cannot tell the user which it was; keep error.message in the details box (already done) so the log line uninstall.helper-stop-failed plus the message stays diagnosable.

title: The quit-required instruction cannot succeed for a normal quit-and-reopen, so the same notice repeats daily
scenario: 1. Discord updates while open; the helper defers (discord-running) and after 30 minutes says quit Discord then open it again. 2. The user does exactly that in about ten seconds. 3. The task runs every 5 minutes (WINDOWS_INTERVAL_SECONDS=300) and a run returns at once when Discord is running, so the closed window of ten seconds is caught with probability of roughly 13s/300s. Even when caught, the settle needs 8s quiet plus a 5s confirm, so a reopen inside 13s is also missed. 4. raiseAlert repeats the same notice 24h later; the diagnostics show the 0.1.3 helper deferring for 11 days on one machine.
whatHappens: The user follows the instruction and nothing changes. Subline stays off until Discord happens to be closed across a 5 minute boundary, and the daily repeat trains them to ignore it.
fix: Two parts. Copy: 'Quit Discord and leave it closed for about a minute before opening it again.' Behaviour: when a repair is pending and Discord is running on win32, stay in the run and re-check discordRunning every 20s for up to 4.5 minutes (one tasklist per 20s only while a repair is pending, not all day for healthy installs), and once closed use a shorter settle for the quit case (the updater already finished; 3s quiet, 2s confirm). Better still, have the mod's main process run `schtasks /Run /TN \Subline\Helper` on Discord's before-quit so the helper starts within seconds of a quit; this is the same hook Vencord uses for its own persistence.
test: tests/helper.test.ts (platform win32): after a wiped injection with discordOpen true, make discordRunning return false 40s into the run (count sleeps); expect report.repatched to contain the install within that single run and the quit-required text to include 'leave it closed'. Fails on main (deferred, repatched empty).
betterFix: The proposed fix is incomplete and one part is wrong on its own. 1. Do not ship the "leave it closed for about a minute" copy alone. With the 5 minute cadence it is false; it is true only with in-run polling or a quit hook. Ship them together. 2. Primary: the mod's main process (Subline ships Vencord's patcher.js, loaded by the stub, so it has app events) runs `schtasks /Run /TN \Subline\Helper` on `will-quit` (real quit only, not close-to-tray). The helper must then tolerate the exiting process: Discord.exe stays in tasklist for 1 to 3s after will-quit, so on win32 a "discord-running" result must re-poll every 2s for up to 30s before deferring. Note MultipleInstancesPolicy is IgnoreNew (scheduledTask.ts line 152), so a /Run during an in-flight run is dropped; keep runs that defer short so this window is near zero, and keep the fallback below. 3. Fallback for tray users and for the dropped /Run: only while state.installs[id].blockedByRunningSince is set, poll discordRunning every 20s for up to 4 minutes inside the run (ExecutionTimeLimit is PT10M, so this fits). Healthy installs keep one tasklist per run. 4. Remove the need for a quit in the common Squirrel case: on Windows the running OLD Discord does not hold the NEW app-1.0.xxxx folder's app.asar. discordRunning (app/discordProcess.ts findDiscordProcesses) matches image name only, because tasklist gives no path. Add an executable-path lookup (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='Discord.exe'" ExecutablePath) and treat Discord as "running for this install" only when the path is under install.rootPath; fall back to the name match when the lookup fails. Then the repair is written while the user keeps Discord open and the existing restart-required notice applies. 5. Tests (helper.test.ts, platform win32, must fail on main): a) wiped injection, discordOpen true, discordRunning returns false after 40s of counted sleeps: expect repatched in that run and the quit-required text to contain "leave it closed"; b) helper run triggered 1s after quit with discordRunning true for the first two polls then false: expect repatched, no deferral; c) two app folders, process path under the old folder: expect the new folder patched with Discord "running" and a restart-required notice, no quit-required; d) healthy install with Discord open: expect at most 2 discordRunning calls per run (keeps the existing cost guard).

title: repatch-failed, rollback-failed and backup-missing are never cleared when the app repairs the install, and the durable alert file is read by nothing
scenario: 1. Two failed repatches raise repatch-failed (helper.ts:774) with 'Open Subline to finish.' 2. The user opens Subline, the install flow patches, translation works. 3. Every later helper run takes the not-needed branch (helper.ts:550-574), which clears only restart-required and quit-required; the three failure codes are cleared only on the helper's own successful patch (helper.ts:624-626). alerts.json keeps repatch-failed with a growing count forever. The same holds for backup-missing after the user reinstalls Discord and Subline as told. 4. Separately, main.ts registers helper:alerts and readPendingAlerts, but preload.cts exposes nothing for it and renderer.ts never calls it, so the durable surface alerts.ts describes as 'the one that survives being missed' is never shown.
whatHappens: A notification missed under Do Not Disturb or sleep is lost, and the record that should replace it either does not reach the user or states a failure that was fixed days ago. The helper's own memory then lies to anyone reading alerts.json or the diagnostics.
fix: In the not-needed branch call run.clear for repatch-failed, rollback-failed and backup-missing: a verified patch is proof those conditions ended. Then either wire helper:alerts through preload and show pending alerts on the already-installed and welcome screens, or delete readPendingAlerts and the IPC handler so the design does not claim a surface that does not exist.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: force two patch failures to raise repatch-failed, then call patchInstall directly (the app's path), run the helper, and expect a decision 'repatch-failed:resolved' and readPendingAlerts(productDir) to be empty. Fails on main.
betterFix: Proposed fix is right but incomplete. In the not-needed branch (helper.ts:603-627) also: (a) run.clear("repatch-failed"), run.clear("rollback-failed"), run.clear("backup-missing"), since a verified patch is proof the condition ended; this also covers the re-adopt path, which falls into the same branch after decideRepatch re-runs; (b) reset the per-install failures counter to 0 in rememberInstall when reason is none (a verified patch ends the failure streak), so one later failure does not alert immediately. For the IPC: either wire it (preload: pendingAlerts: () => ipcRenderer.invoke("helper:alerts"); renderer: on the already-installed and welcome screens show a fixed sentence per code, mapping rollback-failed and backup-missing to the reinstall-Discord remedy and repatch-failed to the repair button) or delete readPendingAlerts, the handler at main.ts:464 and the 'durable surface' paragraph in alerts.ts. Do not have the app write helper-state.json itself: the helper may be mid-run (WatchPaths fires on the app's own patch write on macOS), and the helper's next run now clears it. Tests (fail on current branch): tests/helper.test.ts: two failing runs, then patchInstall directly, advance, harness.run(); expect a 'repatch-failed:resolved' decision, readPendingAlerts(productDir) empty, and readState().installs[id].failures === 0. Same shape for backup-missing (restore the backup file and marker by hand after the alert, then run). If wiring the IPC, add a preload/renderer test asserting window.subline.pendingAlerts exists and that the already-installed screen renders the sentence for a seeded alerts.json.

title: Vencord's host-update persistence copies our stub into the new app-1.0.x folder without the marker (the Windows marker loss)
scenario: 1. Subline patches app-1.0.9259 (stub + subline-patch.json + _app.asar). 2. Discord downloads 1.0.9260 while running; Squirrel extracts a clean app-1.0.9260 (the helper logs injection-wiped, deferred because Discord is open: diagnostics 10-04 13:01). 3. Inside the running old Discord our bundled Vencord's patchLatest fires on the host-updated event and again on before-quit: renameSync(new app.asar -> _app.asar) then copyFileSync(old app.asar -> new app.asar). It copies the stub only. 4. User reopens Discord; 1.0.9260 now carries our stub, a backup, and no marker. 5. Every helper run: state.ts classifyStub sees marker null, identifyModFromLoaderPath('...\Subline\mod\patcher.js') = unknown, so kind=patched-by-other, helper.ts:471 logs foreign-mod and abandons it (diagnostics 10-05 10:01 onward); checkHealth has no marker so it is blind; the installer shows mod-conflict; uninstall refuses with FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (diagnostics 10-06 12:08).
whatHappens: Translation keeps working by accident (the copied stub loads our loader) but Subline no longer knows the install is its own: no marker, no health, no repatch on the next update, and no uninstall. The shipped loader proves it: `grep 'Detected Host Update' installer/build/mod/patcher.js` matches, and buildMod.mjs rewrites settings.tsx only, never src/main. Note the owner's Windows machine runs the 0.1.3 helper (product=0.1.3 in the log, hourly task, 5 minute in-run wait). A helper-side fix reaches it only after reinstalling the app; a mod-side fix reaches it through the feed.
fix: Keep the persistence (it is the fastest Windows self-heal there is) but make it carry ownership and make the helper adopt its result. (a) In scripts/buildMod.mjs add an anchored source rewrite of persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts, failing the build if the anchor is missing like the existing replace() helper: after `copyFileSync(oldVencordAsar, newAppAsar);` insert `const m = "subline-patch.json"; if (existsSync(join(oldResources, m))) copyFileSync(join(oldResources, m), join(resources, m));`. (b) In the helper, with the in-progress own-loader classification, add a marker-only repair: when the stub already verifies (stubIndexSource or legacyStubIndexSource for bundle.loaderPath, STUB_PACKAGE_JSON, _app.asar present and original) and only the marker is missing or records another loaderPath/pluginBuildId/discordVersion, write the marker with writeMarker and do not touch app.asar. Give patchInstall this fast path (return a report with markerOnly: true) and in reconcile pass requireDiscordClosed: false for that reason, since Discord never opens the sidecar. (c) Document in docs/RELEASING.md that the mod build must keep the marker copy in persistence.
test: tests/bundle.test.ts or a new tests/buildMod.test.ts: run the rewrite function on the pinned persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts text and assert the result copies subline-patch.json next to the app.asar copy, and that the rewrite throws when the anchor is absent. tests/helper.test.ts (platform win32, Discord open): write buildStubAsar(runtimeDir/patcher.js) over app.asar, keep _app.asar, delete the marker, run the helper; expect managed=1, readMarker ok with pluginBuildId = bundle.buildId, app.asar bytes and mtime unchanged, no quit-required after 8 runs over 40 minutes, and no FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT from unpatchInstall. Both fail on main.
betterFix: Keep (a) but write a fresh marker instead of copying bytes, and make stale markers self-heal. 1. Build rewrite (installer/scripts/buildMod.mjs, anchored on `copyFileSync(oldVencordAsar, newAppAsar);`, fail the build if the anchor is missing, same style as the settings.tsx replace helper): after the asar copy, in its own try/catch so a marker failure never aborts the asar copy, read `join(oldResources, "subline-patch.json")` with original-fs; if it parses and product === "subline", write it to `join(resources, "subline-patch.json")` with discordVersion = latestVersion.slice(4), backupPath = newAppAsarBackup, patchedAt = new Date().toISOString(), keeping format, productVersion, loaderPath and pluginBuildId. Put the rewrite in an exported pure function (e.g. installer/scripts/vencordRewrites.mjs) so a test can run it on the pinned source text and assert the inserted block plus the throw when the anchor is absent. 2. Patcher: in state.ts classifyStub add a `marker-stale` warning when the marker's backupPath is non-empty and does not normalise to install.backupPath (reuse normaliseLoaderPath) or marker.discordVersion differs from the folder's version; include it in needsMarkerRewrite so adoptPatch (marker-only, Discord may run) rewrites discordVersion, backupPath and patchedAt. This also covers bundles already in the field that will copy verbatim, and markers copied by hand. 3. Tests: helper.test.ts win32 + Discord open: copy the old folder's marker verbatim into the new app-x folder; expect scan re-adopt, marker discordVersion = new version, backupPath = new folder, patchedAt >= now, app.asar bytes/mtime unchanged, and checkHealth rejecting a beacon older than the re-adopt. Keep the finding's proposed marker-deleted test (already covered on the branch at helper.test.ts:449) and add the buildMod rewrite test. 4. docs/RELEASING.md: note the persistence rewrite must survive a Vencord pin bump (the build fails on a missing anchor by design).

title: After a mod update under an open Discord, the helper nags 'Discord updated, quit Discord' daily for a change that only needs the marker rewritten
scenario: 1. Discord is open (tray) and healthy, patched with build A. 2. Trigger B installs build B into the bundle dir (the diagnostics show three such installs on 09-24, 09-25 and 10-04 with repatch deferred each time). 3. Next run: decideRepatch sees patched-by-us, verifyPatch fails only on marker.pluginBuildId, returns build-changed. 4. reconcile calls awaitDiscordSettled with requireDiscordClosed on win32, gets discord-running at once, defers, and noteBlockedByRunningDiscord starts the 30 minute clock. 5. After 30 minutes the user gets 'Discord updated. To turn Subline back on, right-click the Discord icon near the clock, choose Quit Discord, then open Discord again.' 6. They quit and reopen within seconds; the 5 minute task never sees Discord closed; raiseAlert repeats the same text every 24h while blocked. The in-progress re-adoption fix produces the same loop for a missing marker.
whatHappens: The notice is false twice: Discord did not update, and Subline is on (the running Discord keeps build A, the next launch loads build B from the unchanged loader path). The only thing out of date is the sidecar, which Discord never opens. The user is told to do something that does not work and is told again every day.
fix: Add RepatchReason 'marker-stale' to decideRepatch: stub verifies for bundle.loaderPath (either known stub source) and _app.asar is the original, only the marker differs. For that reason pass requireDiscordClosed: false to awaitDiscordSettled and call a marker-only write (see finding 1b), never the asar path; never raise quit-required for it. Keep restart-required with the existing 'Subline updated' text and key so it fires once. Only injection-wiped, patch-damaged and broken-install may raise quit-required, and the text must name the real cause (noteBlockedByRunningDiscord gets the reason).
test: tests/helper.test.ts (platform win32, discordOpen true): patchForReal, run, rebuild shipped bundle to a new buildId and installModBundle, then run 8 times over 40 minutes; expect the marker's pluginBuildId to equal the new buildId after the first run, app.asar bytes unchanged, notifications to contain no quit-required and exactly one restart-required with message 'Subline updated. Quit and reopen Discord to use the new version.' Fails on main (quit-required after 30 minutes, marker still old).
betterFix:
The proposed fix is right in direction but should live in the patcher as well as the helper, and should reuse the branch's existing pre-settle adopt block instead of a second awaitDiscordSettled call.

1. Patcher (installer/src/patcher/patch.ts): add a predicate markerStale(state, bundle): kind patched-by-us, state.loaderPath === bundle.loaderPath, state.marker?.pluginBuildId !== bundle.buildId. adoptPatch accepts a third warning "marker-stale" (AdoptReport.warning union). Check the stub form and the backup BEFORE writing the marker (verifyPatch with the marker's current build id, or move those checks ahead of writeMarker), so a damaged stub is refused with NOT_ADOPTABLE without touching the marker. patchInstall's adopt branch uses needsMarkerRewrite(state) || markerStale(state, bundle), so the installer app's own repatch also stops rewriting app.asar for a Subline-only update and no longer needs Discord quit on Windows for it.

2. Helper (installer/src/helper/helper.ts decideRepatch): for patched-by-us with a failed verifyPatch, return "marker-stale" when verifyPatch(install, { loaderPath: bundle.loaderPath, buildId: entry.marker?.pluginBuildId }) passes (everything but the build id is right). Keep "build-changed" only when something else also differs. In reconcile, extend the existing pre-settle adopt block (reason === "marker-missing") to marker-stale; no awaitDiscordSettled for it on either OS, since the marker is a sidecar Discord never opens. After a successful marker-stale adoption, if Discord is running, raise restart-required once with "Subline updated. Quit and reopen Discord to use the new version." and key `${discordVersion}|${bundle.buildId}` (same key scheme as the patch path so the darwin test "a new Subline build under a running Discord says Subline updated" stays green), then continue down the reason-none path. If adoption fails, fall through to the full path as now.

3. noteBlockedByRunningDiscord(run, entry, blocked, reason): "Discord updated..." text only for injection-wiped; patch-damaged, broken-install and a failed adoption get "Subline needs to repair Discord. Right-click the Discord icon near the clock, choose Quit Discord, then open Discord again." Never raise quit-required for marker-stale.

4. Tests (tests/helper.test.ts): the finding's win32 test as written (marker equals new buildId after run 1, app.asar bytes unchanged, no quit-required, exactly one restart-required with the Subline text; fails on the branch today). Plus: the same on darwin asserting app.asar bytes unchanged; adoption refused (marker dir read-only, or stub damaged) falls through and the quit-required text names Subline, not Discord; a patch.test.ts case where patchInstall with a stale marker writes only the marker (alreadyPatched false, app.asar bytes unchanged).

title: Sticky erroring or suspect health makes every 5 minute run a full log entry, so the rotated log keeps only about five days
scenario: 1. verifyOnce reports loaded-erroring whenever the beacon has an error since the patch and nothing rendered yet (common: the owner's log shows errorCode=rate-limited repeatedly), or translating-not-rendering. 2. isIdleRun treats any health other than healthy, quiet or unknown as not idle, so concludeHelperLog writes the header plus every decision (about 1KB) on every run. 3. On Windows that is 288 runs a day, about 300KB a day; the active file rotates at 512KB with 3 generations (log.ts:103-104).
whatHappens: The install and uninstall records that 'Copy diagnostics' exists to carry age out of the log in under a week while nothing is wrong, which is the exact loss quiet.ts was written to prevent.
fix: In isIdleRun treat erroring and suspect as idle when report.health.status equals the previous run's state.health.lastStatus and the observation count did not reach the escalation; log the status change once and the escalation in full.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: write a beacon with lastError since patch, run twice; the second report with unchanged health passes isIdleRun. Fails on main.
betterFix: Compute the change inside observeHealth (health.ts), which still has `previous`: add `changed: boolean` (previous.lastStatus !== status) to HealthObservation. In isIdleRun and isRepeatDeferralRun: a health status of erroring, suspect or broken is idle when `changed === false && escalated === false`; the first run that enters each status, any transition, and the escalation to broken log in full. Keep the helper.idle line carrying `summary` (it already says "health erroring"/"health broken"), so every run still leaves one dated line with the status. Tests: health.test.ts: second consecutive loaded-erroring observation has changed=false, first has changed=true, suspect->broken has escalated=true; fastRepatch.test.ts:263: broken with changed=false is idle, broken with escalated=true or changed=true is not; helper.test.ts: beacon with lastError since patch, run twice 5 minutes apart, first report fails isIdleRun, second passes; and the same for translating-not-rendering across 72 runs where only run 1 and the escalating run write a full entry (count writeHeader calls via concludeHelperLog). All fail on main because HealthObservation has no `changed` and isIdleRun rejects the status.

title: update-failed repeats every day forever for a permanently unreachable feed, and gives a useless remedy for a manifest format bump
scenario: 1. The feed is unreachable for good (corporate proxy, GitHub blocked by region) or a future release bumps the manifest format so parseReleaseManifest returns RELEASE_MALFORMED 'Update Subline itself' (release.ts:162-168), which only reaches the log. 2. Every 6 hours failUpdate increments updateFailures; from the third failure on it raises update-failed and raiseAlert notifies once per 24h with 'Subline has not been able to check for updates ... open Subline.' 3. Opening Subline changes nothing in either case; the app never auto-updates.
whatHappens: A daily notification for the life of the install, with no action that resolves it. For the format case the one action that would help (download the new Subline) is never said.
fix: Cap notifications per failure code: after the first update-failed notification, notify again only when the error code changes or after 7 days, while still logging every failure. For RELEASE_MALFORMED caused by format mismatch use a distinct message: 'This version of Subline can no longer read its update feed. Download the new Subline from the site.' Add to docs/RELEASING.md: the manifest format and the bundle manifest format are compatibility contracts with every shipped app; never bump either without keeping the old one served.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: feed returns NETWORK_ERROR on 40 runs spaced 6h apart with forceUpdateCheck; expect exactly 2 update-failed notifications in 10 days. With a format 2 manifest expect the message to mention downloading the new Subline. Both fail on main.
betterFix: Keep the 7-day cap and the distinct message, but do not key the alert on the error code. raiseAlert treats a changed key as a new event and notifies immediately, bypassing the window. A corporate proxy or captive portal that alternates between a refused connection (NETWORK_ERROR) and an HTML page (RELEASE_MALFORMED from JSON.parse) would then notify every 6 hours, worse than today. Instead: (a) add "update-failed": 7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000 to REPEAT_MS_BY_CODE in alerts.ts, no key; (b) give the format mismatch its own error code (e.g. RELEASE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED) in parseReleaseManifest so failUpdate can pick the message by code without string matching; a captive-portal HTML page must stay RELEASE_MALFORMED and keep the generic text; (c) message for the new code: 'This Subline can no longer read its update feed. Get the new Subline from surfer05.github.io/subline.' (the site, never a release URL, per the download-site rule); (d) treat RELEASE_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED like RELEASE_UNVERIFIED and alert on the first failure, since it is deterministic and will never recover on its own; (e) add the compatibility-contract paragraph to docs/RELEASING.md section 4 and to packaging/manifest.ts; (f) either wire the renderer to helper:alerts or delete the handler and the 'app shows it on next open' claim in alerts.ts, because today it is dead. Tests in installer/tests/helper.test.ts: 40 runs 6h apart with feed = NETWORK_ERROR, expect exactly 2 notifications and 40 'update failed' decisions in the log; feed with format 2, expect one notification on the first run whose message contains 'surfer05.github.io/subline'; feed alternating NETWORK_ERROR and a RELEASE_MALFORMED HTML body every run for 10 days, expect at most 2 notifications (this third test is what catches the keyed-on-code version).

title: The helper's own memory is the only ownership record consulted, so a lost helper-state.json plus a Discord update means silent abandonment
scenario: 1. helper-state.json is missing or unparseable (deleted by a cleaner, a product folder restored from a backup, a hand edit; parseHelperState returns the empty state). 2. Discord updates and wipes stub and marker. 3. collectManaged: oursNow false, oursOnce false, logs not-ours and skips. The installer's own record patched-installs.json (written on every successful patch, read by locate for remembered paths) is never consulted for ownership.
whatHappens: Translation stops after the Discord update and nothing repairs or reports it; the log reads exactly like a machine where Subline was never installed, which is the failure the diagnostics show for the 0.1.0 helper for days.
fix: Treat the stableIds in patched-installs.json as ownership evidence in collectManaged (pass readPatchedInstalls through a port), and have the helper re-seed helper-state.json from it when the state file is empty. Also have the installer seed helper-state.json installs[stableId] at patch time so the first helper run is never the first memory.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: patchForReal, delete helper-state.json, write patched-installs.json with the fixture's stableId, simulate a Discord update, run; expect repatched to contain the install. Fails on main (not-ours).
betterFix: The proposed fix is right. Make it concrete and close the first-run gap in the same change. 1. HelperPorts gets `rememberedStableIds?(): ReadonlySet<string>`; the real port returns the stableIds from readPatchedInstalls(productDir). collectManaged: `oursOnce = remembered !== undefined || ports.rememberedStableIds?.().has(install.stableId) === true`. Keep the patched-by-other and other-account checks after it, so the record never overrides a foreign mod. Log a new decision `remembered-by-installer` so a run that relied on it is diagnosable. 2. When the helper state is empty and the record names the install, re-seed state.installs[stableId] with discordVersion from the marker or readDiscordVersion and buildId null; rememberInstall then writes it on the normal path. 3. In the installer, make ports.rememberPatchedInstall also write helper-state.json installs[stableId] = {discordVersion, buildId, patchedAt, failures: 0} before installHelper runs (flow.ts already orders remember before installHelper). Read the existing state first and merge, never overwrite other keys. 4. main.ts 438 managedResources: union readState().installs keys with readPatchedInstalls stableIds, so macOS WatchPaths also survive a lost state file. 5. Tests: (a) helper.test.ts: patchForReal, run, delete helper-state.json, stub rememberedStableIds to the fixture's stableId, simulateDiscordUpdate, run; expect repatched to contain the install and no not-ours line. Fails on the branch today. (b) The first-run case: patchForReal without any helper run, simulateDiscordUpdate, run with the seeded state the installer now writes; expect repatched. (c) Guard: foreign stub plus the stableId in both records still logs foreign-mod and repatched is empty. (d) Uninstall test: after uninstall neither file exists, and a helper run with the removed task logs nothing and writes nothing.

title: Helper is removed before the Discord-running and restore checks; a refused or failed uninstall leaves Discord patched with no helper and says nothing changed
scenario: User presses Uninstall while Discord is open (Windows: in the tray). main.ts:606 removeHelperFor() deletes the scheduled task / LaunchAgent. Only then main.ts:648 lists processes and uninstall.ts:242-265 refuses with DISCORD_RUNNING, 'Nothing has been changed'. The user closes Subline, or the retry fails (FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT, FILE_IN_USE, BACKUP_MISSING, PERMISSION_DENIED): Discord is still patched, the helper is gone. Owner's log shows it five times: lines 35-39, 70-74, 138-142, 1594-1600 (helperRemoved=true then DISCORD_RUNNING; retry helperRemoved=false then restore-failed FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT; summary claims nothing deleted).
whatHappens: The helper abandons an install it owns: the next Discord update wipes the injection and nothing repairs it (Subline silently stops), and ensureHelperFromHelper never resurrects a removed task/plist. The report lies: summarize() at uninstall.ts:434 says 'Nothing has been deleted' although the helper was removed, some installs may have been restored, and (with keepSettings=false) the settings were deleted. It only self-heals if the user reopens Subline (flow.ts:932 ensureHelper).
fix: Make uninstall() own the ordering: pass ports removeHelper() and restoreHelper() instead of a precomputed HelperRemoval. Order: App Management probe, Discord-running check, THEN remove the helper, THEN restore. After the restore loop, if any target still loads our loader (any restore failed, or no target was restorable) call restoreHelper() (installHelperFor) and report helperStopped=false with 'background updates were put back'. summarize() must read outcomes: helper removed, N of M Discords restored, settings removed; never 'Nothing has been changed' when any of those is true.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: (1) discordRunning non-empty -> removeHelper port not called, report.helperStopped=false is not claimed as removed; (2) one unpatch fails -> restoreHelper called once, report.helperStopped=false, summary matches /updates were put back/; (3) helper.removed=true and restore fails -> summary does not match /Nothing has been (changed|deleted)/. Each fails on main today because the helper removal is outside uninstall().
betterFix: The proposed fix is right. Keep it, with these additions. (1) Move both refusals (helper-stop failure and DISCORD_RUNNING) ahead of every write, including the helper removal: uninstall() takes removeHelper() and restoreHelper() ports and calls removeHelper only after the App Management probe, the optional quitDiscord, and the process list all pass. (2) After the restore loop, if any restore failed or any remembered install is stillMarked, call restoreHelper() and log the outcome; report helperStopped=false and say "background updates were put back so Discord keeps working". If restoreHelper itself fails, say so with the code; never claim the helper is in place. (3) Gate removePluginSettings behind discordRestored the same way product data is gated, or report settingsRemoved honestly; today it deletes the key and the summary says nothing was deleted. (4) summarize() must be built from outcomes: helper removed yes/no/put back, N of M Discords restored, settings removed yes/no. Only emit "Nothing has been changed" when helper.removed is false, restores is empty, and settingsRemoved is false. (5) The helper-stop failure text says "restart your Mac" on Windows too; make it platform aware. (6) Tests: the three in the finding, plus: keepSettings=false with a failed restore must not say "Nothing has been deleted" and must report settingsRemoved truthfully; two installs with one failure must say "1 of 2"; restoreHelper failing must surface its error code in problems. Each test fails on main because helper removal is outside uninstall() and because summarize() ignores helper and settings outcomes.

title: Settings are deleted even when Discord is still patched; the summary then says nothing was deleted
scenario: User chooses OK on 'Remove your settings as well?'. A restore fails (FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT, FILE_IN_USE, BACKUP_MISSING, PERMISSION_DENIED). uninstall.ts:331-334 runs removePluginSettings regardless of discordRestored and deletes the whole VcTranslate block (installId, sublineCode, clearedPurchaseCode, targetLang, engine). Only product data is gated (line 347). Observed 10-06 12:08 (keepSettings=false, restore-failed).
whatHappens: Subline keeps running inside Discord with no settings: the plugin mints a new install id (burns a relay computer slot, see entitle.ts MAX_INSTALLS), the reading language and code are gone, and summarize() line 434 tells the user 'Nothing has been deleted'.
fix: Gate settings removal on discordRestored (remove settings only once Subline is out of every Discord); when kept because of a failed restore, say so. Make the summary read settingsRemoved and the restore outcomes.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: keepSettings=false with unpatchFail -> settings file byte-identical, report.settingsRemoved=false, summary does not match /Nothing has been deleted/. Fails today.
betterFix: Gate on "no Discord still loads Subline", not on discordRestored. discordRestored requires restores.length > 0, so with zero Discord installs and keepSettings=false the proposed gate would never remove settings, and today that same case already keeps the bundle and product folder (modBundleKeptForSafety=true) while the summary says "There was nothing to remove". Define once: const nothingLoadsSubline = restores.every(e => e.ok) && stillMarked.length === 0 (true for an empty list). Use it for step 2 (bundle), step 3 product data AND settings. Keep discordRestored (restores.length > 0 && ...) only for the summary wording. When settings are kept because a restore failed, log a distinct event (uninstall.settings-kept reason=a Discord still loads Subline) and log the removePluginSettings outcome too, since the field log could not show what happened. Make summarize() take settingsRemoved/productDataRemoved and never print "Nothing has been deleted" unless both are false (with the gate they always are on a failed restore, so the sentence becomes true by construction; add "Your settings were kept so Subline keeps working until you retry"). Tests (installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts): (1) for each of FILE_IN_USE, PERMISSION_DENIED, FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT, BACKUP_MISSING with keepSettings=false: settings.json byte-identical, report.settingsRemoved=false, summary not matching /Nothing has been deleted/ when anything was removed; (2) installs=[] with keepSettings=false and no remembered markers: settings key removed, bundle and product folder removed, summary says so; (3) extend the "whatever happens" matrix to assert the VcTranslate key survives whenever !discordRestored. Neighbour worth a separate finding: stillMarked only checks the marker file, so a remembered Discord whose marker was lost by a Windows update but whose stub still require()s our loader is invisible to step 2 and the bundle can be deleted under it; it should also check the stub by own loader path, like the implementer's unpatch fix now does.

title: Any _app.asar counts as Subline residue, so a Vencord or Equicord PTB/Canary or a leftover Windows folder makes uninstall fail forever and keeps the bundle
scenario: Subline on Discord Stable; Vencord on Discord PTB (or an old app-1.0.X folder that Vencord patched before Subline). uninstallTargets (locate.ts:383) sweeps every branch with locatePatchedResidue; carriesOurMark (locate.ts:320-322) is true for a bare _app.asar. The PTB becomes a target; unpatchInstall returns FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (patch.ts:470); uninstall.ts:313 discordRestored=false; bundle and product data kept (uninstall.ts:314-316, 347); clean=false; summary 'could not fully remove itself ... Nothing has been deleted' although Stable was restored and the helper removed.
whatHappens: The user can never get a clean uninstall; several MB of mod bundle, helper state and beacon stay forever; the footer button keeps offering an uninstall that fails the same way; the message blames Discord. The bundle is kept 'for safety' for a Discord that does not load it.
fix: In uninstall(): a FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT from a target that carries no marker and whose stub loader is outside modBundleDir is 'not ours': log uninstall.skipped-foreign, exclude it from restores, and do not count it against discordRestored. Decide modBundleKeptForSafety only from targets whose stub still loads our loader (inspect them after the restore loop instead of checking the marker file). Optionally tighten carriesOurMark to marker OR stub-loads-our-loader.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: targets [stable ok, ptb -> FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT with modName Vencord] -> discordRestored true, modBundleRemoved true, clean true, summary names PTB as left to Vencord. installer/tests/locate.test.ts: a PTB with _app.asar and a Vencord stub is not returned by uninstallTargets (or is flagged foreign). Both fail today.
betterFix: The proposed fix is incomplete in two ways. (1) Its condition "no marker and loader outside modBundleDir" misses the common case Vencord-installed-over-Subline: Vencord's installer leaves our subline-patch.json beside its stub, so the state is patched-by-other with marker-loader-mismatch, and the marker is OURS to remove; that case would still fail. (2) uninstall.ts is deliberately I/O-free (it only takes ports); inspecting stubs there breaks that design and the tests that rely on the fake unpatch port. Do it in the patcher instead: in unpatchInstall, case patched-by-other without removeForeignMod, return ok({ restored:false, alreadyClean:true, previousState:"patched-by-other", foreignMod: state.modName, removedArtifacts:[our stale marker, removed via removeMarker when present], summary:`${modName} is installed here. It was left alone.` }) instead of err FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (its sole caller is main.ts:665; keep the error only for removeForeignMod semantics if ever needed). Add foreignMod?: string to UnpatchReport. In uninstall(): discordRestored stays "every restore ok" (now true), pass foreign names to summarize and append "Discord PTB is modified by Vencord and was left to it. Remove it with Vencord's own uninstaller." Keep the bundle-kept rule for genuine failures of OUR installs only. Optionally tighten carriesOurMark to: marker exists OR stub loads our loader OR (app.asar missing AND _app.asar present); a bare _app.asar beside a real app.asar with no marker is never deleted by cleanUpUnpatched anyway, so listing it only adds permission probes. Tests: patch.test.ts "refuses to uninstall another mod" becomes ok/restored:false/asar hash unchanged/backup kept/our stale marker removed; uninstall.test.ts [stable ok, ptb foreign Vencord] -> discordRestored true, modBundleRemoved true, productDataRemoved true when asked, clean true, summary names PTB and Vencord; locate.test.ts PTB with Vencord stub + _app.asar not listed as residue (if carriesOurMark is tightened); a Windows app-1.0.X older folder holding our stub without a marker is still listed. All fail today.

title: 'Remove settings' deletes the install id; every reinstall takes one of the account's three computer slots and a paying user is locked out for 30 days
scenario: Paid Automatic user. Uninstall with OK deletes plugins.VcTranslate entirely (installId included; the test at uninstall.test.ts:375 asserts this). Reinstall: readPriorUse false -> paid gate -> ensureInstallId generates a new id -> relay joinInstall (relay/src/entitle.ts:206-217, MAX_INSTALLS=3, EVICT_AFTER_MS=30 days). Third cycle within a month: device_limit -> codeScreen.ts:49 'This code is on 3 computers already. It frees up after 30 days unused'. The owner's own log shows six install/uninstall cycles in two days.
whatHappens: A user who paid $4.99 and reinstalled to fix a problem is refused activation for 30 days or has to ask on GitHub for /admin/reset-installs. The dialog text (renderer.ts:721) says only 'OK removes them'.
fix: removePluginSettings keeps installId (and clearedPurchaseCode) and removes everything else; keep readPriorUse false for an id-only block so the fresh-install gate still applies; dialog copy: 'Your purchase stays linked to this computer.' Alternatively add a relay release endpoint called on uninstall. The existing test at line 375 must flip to assert the id survives.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: removePluginSettings leaves plugins.VcTranslate = { installId } and nothing else; installer/tests/language.test.ts: readPriorUse false and readInstallId returns the old id after that removal; a flow test that reinstall after OK reuses the id (ensureInstallId returns it, no newInstallId call). Fails today.
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in direction; tighten it as follows. 1) removePluginSettings: instead of deleting the key, replace the block with only the valid-shaped installId (32 lowercase hex, drop junk) and a non-empty clearedPurchaseCode; delete the key entirely when neither is present. Return ok(false) when the block held nothing besides those two, so the summary's "Your settings were removed" stays true to what happened. Keeping clearedPurchaseCode is essential, not optional: once the id survives, checkSavedInstall gets the purchase code back from the relay and the clearedCode guard (flow.ts:1489) is what stops a reinstall from re-saving a code the reader deliberately cleared. 2) No change to readPriorUse; it already treats an id-only block as no prior use, so the fresh-install gate still applies and the reinstall goes savedInstallId -> checkSavedInstall -> relay confirms Automatic -> activated, with no new id and no new slot. This also closes the double purchase: checkout for the kept id answers already_owned and flow goes to alreadyActivated. 3) Dialog copy (renderer.ts:722): "OK removes your language and other settings. Your purchase stays linked to this computer, so reinstalling will not ask you to pay or enter a code again. Cancel keeps everything." 4) Do not add a relay release endpoint as the fix: releasing the slot on uninstall would make the reinstall ask for a code the user may not have, and the id is 16 random bytes tied to nothing, so keeping it costs nothing. Tests: uninstall.test.ts line 375 flips to assert plugins.VcTranslate equals { installId, clearedPurchaseCode } with sublineCode, targetLang and engine gone; a case with only { installId } returns ok(false) and leaves it; a case with a malformed installId deletes the key; language.test.ts: readInstallId returns the old id and readPriorUse is false after removal; flow.test.ts: after an uninstall with keepSettings false, a new run with hasSublineCode false and savedInstallId set reaches checkSavedInstall and never calls newInstallId, and buyAutomatic on that id gets already_owned rather than a checkout URL.

title: DiagnosticsLog rotation is not safe with two writers, and the installer and the WatchPaths-triggered helper write at the same moment
scenario: 1. The installer patches app.asar; launchd starts the helper within 10s on WatchPaths; both append to subline.log. 2. Both cross the 512KB boundary: both statSync a size over the cap, both shift generations, the second renameSync(path, path.1) throws ENOENT because the first already moved it, or moves the first writer's fresh file over generation 1. 3. append has no try/catch, so in the installer the throw escapes from a log.info call inside applyPatch after patch.ok (flow.ts:1801) and installHelper never runs; the flow stays busy on the patching screen with Discord patched and no helper registered.
whatHappens: A rare but real stuck installer, or a silently lost log generation, caused by the helper being the second writer. The helper side is buffered and flushed late, so it mostly hits the second outcome.
fix: Make DiagnosticsLog.append never throw: wrap rotation and append in try/catch and fall back to appending without rotating. Use a rotation that cannot double-shift: rename to a timestamped name and prune, or re-stat under a lock file.
test: tests/log.test.ts: two DiagnosticsLog instances on one dir with maxBytes small; interleave writes across the boundary and assert neither throws and exactly one rotation happened. Fails on main (ENOENT).
betterFix: 1. log.ts: append and writeHeader must never throw. Wrap rotateIfNeeded in try/catch and fall through to the append; wrap appendFileSync in try/catch too. A log line must never stop an install or a helper run. 2. Single-shift rotation without a lock file: claim the rotation with mkdirSync(path + ".rotating") (atomic; EEXIST means the other process is rotating, so skip rotation and just append); re-stat inside the claim before renaming so a writer that saw the old size does not move the fresh file over generation 1; rmSync the claim dir in finally; break a claim older than about 30 s (crash mid-rotation). Timestamped names are not needed. 3. main.ts helper mode: put app.exit(0) in a finally around the whole run. 4. main.ts whenReady: the header write must not gate createFlow/createWindow (covered by 1, but keep createWindow outside any throwing call). 5. Tests that fail on main: (a) deterministic: pre-create subline.log.1 as a directory with a file in it so renameSync(path, path.1) throws, fill the active file past the cap, then assert log.info does not throw and the line is in the active file; (b) deterministic double-shift: vi.mock node:fs so statSync reports a size over the cap for a path already removed, assert no throw and the line written; (c) two-process stress with execFileSync(process.execPath, ["--experimental-strip-types", writer.mts]) twice in parallel, maxBytes 300, 20000 lines, assert neither child reports a throw and every rotated generation is non-empty (fails on main 3 of 3 runs here); (d) helper: a FlowLogger that throws on first write still ends with app.exit called. Drop the "two instances in one process" test; it passes on main.

title: The Uninstall button has no cancel path: Cancel in 'Remove your settings as well?' still uninstalls, and uninstallStarted leaves the window dead afterwards
scenario: User clicks the footer Uninstall by mistake (it is live on every screen, including Welcome and Finished). The only dialog is confirm('Remove your settings as well? OK removes them. Cancel keeps them'). Cancel -> keepSettings=true -> runUninstall anyway. main.ts:493 sets uninstallStarted=true and flow:start/send/restart return null for the life of the process (359-370), also after a refused or cancelled permission wait.
whatHappens: An accidental click removes Subline with no way to stop it; after any uninstall attempt, including one refused for a running Discord, the user cannot continue or restart the install without quitting Subline. The user is stuck in the app they are looking at.
fix: Replace confirm() with a three-button modal: Cancel (does nothing), Remove and keep settings, Remove everything. In main.ts reset uninstallStarted when the report says cancelled, permissionCheckFailed, or nothing was changed (DISCORD_RUNNING / NOT_WRITABLE), so flow:restart works again.
test: Extract the dialog decision into a pure function (tests/renderer or copy.test.ts): 'cancel' returns null and no uninstall call is made. New main-wiring test: after a report with problems[0].code DISCORD_RUNNING, flow:restart yields a state, not null. Fails today.
betterFix: 1) Dialog: the renderer is sandboxed, so do the three-way choice in main with dialog.showMessageBox (buttons: Cancel, Remove and keep settings, Remove everything; cancelId 0; defaultId 0) behind a new IPC such as uninstall:ask, and keep the decision pure: `uninstallChoice(buttonIndex): null | { keepSettings: boolean }` in a small module (app/uninstallChoice.ts) with a vitest that Cancel returns null and that the renderer-side caller makes no uninstall call on null. 2) Order: compute discordRunning BEFORE removeHelperFor on the first attempt (closeDiscord undefined). If Discord is running, return the DISCORD_RUNNING report without touching the helper; only after the user presses 'Quit Discord and remove' (closeDiscord 'ask') remove the helper and proceed. Also keep the existing refusals (NOT_WRITABLE, permission cancelled, permissionCheckFailed) before the helper is removed, which they already are. Add a report field such as `nothingChanged: true` set only on those early returns, and test in uninstall.test.ts that the helper removal is not invoked when discordRunning is non-empty on the first attempt (fails today, since main removes it unconditionally; move the ordering into a testable function, e.g. app/uninstallRun.ts that main.ts calls with ports). 3) Resume: extract the session gate from main.ts into a pure module (e.g. app/installSession.ts) with `markUninstallStarted()`, `resumeAfter(report)` that returns true only when report.nothingChanged === true, and `mayDriveFlow()`; main's three handlers consult it. Test: after a DISCORD_RUNNING, NOT_WRITABLE, cancelled or permissionCheckFailed report, mayDriveFlow() is true; after a report with any restore performed (clean or not), it stays false. 4) Renderer: on a report with nothingChanged, reset `uninstalling = false` and add a secondary button 'Back' to the action bar that calls api.restart() and renders its state; keep the footer Uninstall live. A report that changed anything keeps the current dead-end behaviour on purpose, since the flow was aborted and Discord may be half restored. 5) Copy: the DISCORD_RUNNING summary must only say 'Nothing has been changed' when that is true, which the reordering in (2) makes true.

title: No Discord found: 'There was nothing to remove' while the bundle and product folder are kept forever with a false safety reason
scenario: User uninstalls or reinstalls Discord first (a common 'clean slate'), then presses Uninstall in Subline, OK to remove settings. installs=[] -> restores empty -> discordRestored=false (line 313) -> modBundleKeptForSafety=true, log 'a Discord is still patched and needs it to start' (316), product-data-kept (347-349), summary 'There was nothing to remove' (420). The helper was already removed (main.ts:606).
whatHappens: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline or ~/Library/Application Support/Subline (mod bundle, helper-state.json, patched-installs.json, status beacon, alerts) can never be removed through the app; the log states a falsehood; a later reinstall reads stale helper state and beacon.
fix: When there are no targets and no remembered Resources folder whose stub loads our loader, treat Discord as restored for the bundle decision: remove the bundle and (if asked) the product data, and say 'No Discord with Subline in it was found. Subline's own files were removed.' Keep the current refusal only when a remembered Discord still loads us.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: installs=[], rememberedResources=[] -> modBundleRemoved true; with keepSettings=false productDataRemoved true and productDir gone; summary does not say 'nothing to remove' when files were removed. Fails today.
betterFix: The proposed direction is right; tighten it in three places. (1) Split the bundle decision from "every target restored": let noDiscordNeedsBundle = restores.every(e => e.ok) && stillMarked.length === 0 (vacuously true for restores=[]); drive modBundleKeptForSafety, product-data removal and clean from that, and keep discordRestored only for wording. (2) Make the stillMarked check stronger than the marker, because the known field bug is a lost marker: for each remembered Resources folder not restored here, treat it as still patched when the marker exists OR _app.asar exists OR app.asar/index.js parses (parseRequirePath / the ownLoaderPaths check main.ts already hands to unpatch) to our loader. Pass ownLoaderPaths into UninstallOptions so uninstall.ts can run that check without I/O knowledge of the layout. If any remembered Discord still loads us but is not in installs, keep the bundle and say which path. (3) Summary and state: when restores.length===0 and nothing was still marked, return "No Discord with Subline in it was found. Subline's own files were removed." when modBundleRemoved || productDataRemoved, and the existing "There was nothing to remove." only when neither existed; set clean=true in both cases so the renderer shows "Removed" and retires the Uninstall button. Log "uninstall.no-discord" instead of the false "bundle-kept" reason. Residual worst case to state in the comment, not hide: a Discord at a location that is neither default nor remembered (patched-installs.json deleted or corrupt) that still carries a LEGACY single-require stub (pre fail-open, stub.ts:59) will not start after the bundle is removed; the current stub (stub.ts:51-54) falls back to _app.asar, so only legacy stubs are exposed. Tests (installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts, fail today): installs=[], rememberedResources=[missing path], keepSettings=false -> modBundleRemoved true, productDataRemoved true, productDir gone, clean true, summary contains "own files were removed" and not "nothing to remove", log has no "uninstall.bundle-kept"; same with keepSettings=true -> bundle gone, productDir kept; installs=[] with a remembered Resources whose app.asar stub loads our loader but has no marker -> bundle kept, summary names the path; installs=[] with no bundle and no product dir -> summary "nothing to remove", clean true. On Windows (logDir inside productDir) assert the logs folder survives.

title: Windows NSIS uninstaller (Apps & Features) deletes Subline.exe but leaves Discord patched, the mod bundle in place and the scheduled task pointing at nothing; same orphan when Subline.app is trashed on macOS
scenario: User uninstalls Subline the way Windows teaches: Settings > Apps > Subline > Uninstall. installer.nsh defines customCheckAppRunning and customInstall only; there is no customUnInstall, electron-builder.js:294 deleteAppDataOnUninstall is false, and main.ts:127 knows only --helper. Subline.exe and shortcuts are deleted; %LOCALAPPDATA%\Subline\mod, the stub in Discord and the \Subline\Helper task survive. macOS: dragging Subline.app to the Trash leaves ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.subline.helper.plist pointing at a missing binary and Discord still loading the mod.
whatHappens: Discord keeps running Subline after the user 'uninstalled' it; Task Scheduler fails every 5 minutes; nothing ever updates the mod, so the first Discord frontend change leaves a plugin that loads and renders nothing (or errors), and Vencord's persist hook keeps re-injecting the stub on every Discord update. The user has no uninstall left except reinstalling Subline. The in-app Removed screen (renderer.ts:583) never tells the user to remove the app, and INSTALL-NOTE.md never says not to delete it first.
fix: Add a headless mode to main.ts (--uninstall, keepSettings=true, closeDiscord 'ask') that runs uninstall:run's logic and exits 0 only when report.clean or nothing was installed. Add !macro customUnInstall in installer.nsh that ExecWaits '"$INSTDIR\${APP_EXECUTABLE_FILENAME}" --uninstall' before files are removed and, on non-zero exit, shows a MessageBox 'Quit Discord and run Subline, then Uninstall inside it' and Aborts. On the Removed screen add 'You can now delete Subline' (Trash / Windows Settings); add the same to INSTALL-NOTE.md and the site.
test: installer/tests/packaging.test.ts: installer.nsh contains customUnInstall invoking --uninstall and Abort on failure. New test for the headless runner (ports injected): returns exit 0 for clean, non-zero with the refusal summary for DISCORD_RUNNING; it removes the task before restoring. renderer copy test: the clean report's screen contains the delete-the-app sentence.
betterFix: The proposed hook is in the wrong place. In app-builder-lib 25.1.8 templates/nsis/uninstaller.nsh the customUnInstall macro is inserted at line 238, AFTER "RMDir /r $INSTDIR" (line 168) and after the registry keys are deleted, so ExecWait '"$INSTDIR\Subline.exe" --uninstall' would run against a file that no longer exists and the Abort would leave a half-deleted install with no Uninstall entry. Use customUnInit instead (inserted in un.onInit, line 26, before anything is touched) and guard it with ${ifNot} ${isUpdated}: electron-builder runs the OLD uninstaller with --updated during every Subline upgrade, so an unguarded hook would unpatch Discord (and could Abort the upgrade) on every Subline update. Shape: !macro customUnInit / ${ifNot} ${isUpdated} / ExecWait '"$INSTDIR\${APP_EXECUTABLE_FILENAME}" --uninstall' $0 / ${if} $0 != 0 MessageBox "..." + Abort / ${endIf} / !macroend. ExecWait is synchronous, so customCheckAppRunning's taskkill (which runs later in the Section in assisted mode) cannot kill the headless run. The headless --uninstall mode in main.ts must call app.exit(code) explicitly, must not create a window, must return 0 for "nothing was there to remove" (summarize's first branch) and for report.clean, and non-zero otherwise with report.summary logged; keepSettings=true. Do not pass closeDiscord "ask" silently: add an NSIS MessageBox (MB_OKCANCEL) "Subline will close Discord to restore it" before the ExecWait, and only then let the headless run request the polite quit; a forced close must stay GUI-only. Also handle --uninstall /S (silent) by refusing with exit code and no MessageBox. macOS has no hook, so fix it from the helper side: (1) treat process.execPath under "/.Trash/" like /Volumes/ and /AppTranslocation/ in ensureHelperFor AND ensureHelperFromHelper (ports.ts:296 and :380), so a trashed app is never re-registered; (2) when a helper run starts from /.Trash/, do not repatch; instead run the uninstall ordering (remove helper first, restore installs, remove bundle) and log it, since launchd keeps executing the trashed binary until the Trash is emptied. Copy: on the clean Removed screen add "You can now delete Subline from Applications" / "You can now uninstall Subline from Windows Settings", and put the ordering (run Uninstall inside Subline first, then delete the app) in docs/INSTALL-NOTE.md and site/index.html. Tests: packaging.test.ts asserts installer.nsh contains "!macro customUnInit", the isUpdated guard, "--uninstall", "Abort", and does NOT put the ExecWait in customUnInstall; a headless-runner test with injected ports covers exit 0 (clean, nothing-installed), non-zero with DISCORD_RUNNING summary, and that the task is removed before any restore; ports tests cover the ~/.Trash guard for both ensure functions; a helper test covers "run from Trash performs uninstall, never repatch"; a renderer copy test covers the delete-the-app sentence per OS.

title: Every 'this Discord is not ours' decision is logged without the evidence that decided it, and in 0.2.1 the whole run is collapsed to one 'helper.idle' line, so the next marker loss will be undiagnosable from the log
scenario: 1. A located Discord is skipped as 'not-ours' (helper.ts:453), 'foreign-mod' (helper.ts:474) or 'other-account' (helper.ts:465); the decision carries only path, kind and modName, not whether a marker existed, what loader the stub and the marker named, or whether _app.asar was present. 2. In 0.2.1, such a run has no repatch, deferral, failure, update or alert, so isIdleRun (quiet.ts:57-65) returns true and concludeHelperLog (main.ts:185) writes only 'helper.idle summary=Subline is not installed in any Discord that could be found. managed=0'. The held 'foreign-mod' line is discarded (bufferedLogger is never flushed). 3. The field bug in diagnostics.txt was only reconstructable because the owner's app is 0.1.3 (unbuffered); the root cause still had to be proved by reading the bundled Vencord source rather than the log.
whatHappens: A found-but-unmanaged Discord (found > 0, managed === 0) is the signature of every abandonment bug in this family, and the current log hides both the fact and its cause. The project's own rule (memory: diagnosable failures, always log the cause) is not met for the decision that matters most.
fix: 1. In classifyStub return structured evidence on the InstallState: ownership: { markerPresent, markerLoader, stubLoader, backupPresent, decidedBy: 'marker-match' | 'own-loader' | 'marker-missing' | 'marker-mismatch' | 'stub-unparseable' } and have the helper's not-ours / foreign-mod / other-account decisions log those fields. 2. In isIdleRun and isRepeatDeferralRun, treat report.found > report.managed as not idle (or emit one 'helper.unmanaged' line per skipped install with path, kind and the ownership fields, de-duplicated against lastDeferralKey-style memory so it does not repeat every 5 minutes).
test: tests/fastRepatch.test.ts: a report with found 1, managed 0 and a 'scan foreign-mod' decision must not be idle (currently isIdleRun returns true). tests/helper.test.ts: for the Vencord-copied fixture (stub, backup, no marker) assert the logged decision fields include markerPresent=false and stubLoader equal to the bundle's loader path. tests/state.test.ts: classifyStub exposes ownership.decidedBy for each of the five cases.
betterFix: Smaller than proposed, and it must not undo the quiet-log purpose. 1. Do not add a new 'ownership' object to InstallState; the fields already exist. In collectManaged, build one evidence object from the state and attach it to every skip decision (not-ours, other-account, foreign-mod) and to re-adopt: { kind: state.kind, mod: state.mod, loader: state.loaderPath, markerPresent: state.marker !== null, markerLoader: state.marker?.loaderPath ?? null, backup: state.hasBackup, stub: state.asarIsStub, warnings: state.warnings.join(','), remembered: oursOnce }. 2. In isIdleRun, a run with report.found > report.managed is not idle ONLY when the skipped set changed since the last run. Add state.lastUnmanagedKey (same pattern as lastDeferralKey, helper.ts:341) built from sorted 'stableId:outcome:kind:loader' of every skipped install; set report.repeatUnmanaged like repeatDeferral. isIdleRun returns false when found > managed and repeatUnmanaged !== true. Otherwise a user who legitimately runs BetterDiscord would get a full header plus a dozen lines every 5 minutes on Windows, which is the exact log-rotation problem quiet.ts exists to prevent. 3. When the run is collapsed (idle or repeat), still include found in the one line: 'helper.idle summary=... found=1 managed=0', so even the collapsed line shows the signature. Tests: quiet.ts, a report with found 1, managed 0, repeatUnmanaged undefined is not idle; the same with repeatUnmanaged true is idle; the idle line carries found. helper.test.ts, a located install the memory does not know with a patched-by-other state logs 'not-ours' with markerPresent, loader, backup and remembered=false; the same install skipped twice sets repeatUnmanaged on the second run and a different skipped set clears it.

title: Helper cannot repair a half-patched install (app.asar gone, _app.asar present) and its alert then claims 'Discord itself is fine' while Discord cannot start; the installer offers no repair for it either
scenario: How the state arises in the field: Vencord's host-update hook does renameSync(newAppAsar, newAppAsarBackup) then copyFileSync(old, new) inside Discord's before-quit (persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts:62-63); the updater terminates Discord right after before-quit, or the copy fails (antivirus holding the old stub, disk full), leaving app-1.0.9260 with _app.asar and no app.asar. Also any Subline patch interrupted between its two renames (patch.ts:243 and 253) by a kill (schtasks /End during uninstall, ExecutionTimeLimit, power loss). Then: 1. inspectInstall -> broken 'asar-missing-backup-present' (state.ts:159-166). 2. Helper: remembered -> managed -> 'broken-install' -> patchInstall -> guardPatchable returns BROKEN_INSTALL (patch.ts:159-161). 3. handlePatchFailure: BROKEN_INSTALL is in IMMEDIATE_PATCH_ALERTS so it notifies 'Discord updated and Subline could not put its translation back. Discord itself is fine. Open Subline to finish.' (helper.ts:774-781) although it just logged discordStartable=false. 4. The user opens Subline: flow.ts:795-803 shows 'Discord is half-patched ... It can be repaired' with actions retry and cancel only; Try again re-inspects and shows the same screen. Only Uninstall (unpatchBroken -> restoreOriginal, patch.ts:516-524) would fix it, and nothing says so.
whatHappens: Discord does not start (no app.asar), the helper tells the user Discord is fine, and the app offers no button that repairs it. The user is stuck unless they guess that Uninstall is the repair.
fix: 1. patchInstall: treat 'asar-missing-backup-present' as a resumable patch: when state.reason is that and readIsOriginalAsar(backupPath) is true, skip step 2 (backup already there), write the stub to app.asar, write the marker, verify. 2. handlePatchFailure: when discordStartable is false use a different sentence ('Discord cannot start until this is fixed. Open Subline and choose Repair.') and alert immediately. 3. flow.ts broken-install for reasons asar-missing-backup-present and our-patch-without-backup: add a 'repair' action that calls the patcher's restoreOriginal (or re-patch) and then re-inspects; keep the existing refusal for asar-and-backup-missing with the reinstall sentence.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: patch the fixture, then unlinkSync(install.asarPath) leaving _app.asar; run the helper; expect repatched to contain the install, inspectInstall kind patched-by-us, and no 'repatch-failed' alert. tests/patch.test.ts: patchInstall on that state returns ok with backupCreated false and verifies. tests/flow.test.ts: reach broken-install with that reason and assert actions include 'repair' and that sending it leaves the install patched-by-us or unpatched (never broken). Copy test: the helper's failure alert must not say 'Discord itself is fine' when discordStartable is false (without the fix the string is unconditional).
betterFix: The proposed fix is right in direction but incomplete in three places. (a) Fix 1 cannot reuse applyPatch as is: broken() reports asarIsStub=false, so currentIsOriginal=true and the rename of a missing app.asar throws, and if a stray file existed it would clobber the real backup. Add an explicit resume branch: when state.reason==='asar-missing-backup-present' and readIsOriginalAsar(backupPath) is ok and true, write the stub to a temp file, renameSync it onto app.asar, write the marker, verifyPatch; on any failure unlink app.asar and remove the marker so the install returns to the same recoverable state. Invert tests/patch.test.ts:366 to expect ok with backupCreated=false. Keep the guard for asar-and-backup-missing, asar-unreadable, asar-inaccessible, marker-unreadable and foreign-patch-without-backup. (b) Helper: 'Discord cannot start' outranks 'put the patch back'. When the resume patch fails and brokenReason is asar-missing-backup-present, call unpatch (restoreOriginal) so Discord starts, then alert. Use a new alert code (for example 'discord-unstartable') with its own cadence in alerts.ts rather than reusing repatch-failed's 12h throttle, choose the sentence by brokenReason not by a string flag, and run.clear it after a later success. Add a copy test asserting the message never contains 'Discord itself is fine' when discordStartable is false (helper.test.ts:869 keeps the sentence for the VERIFICATION_FAILED case where Discord is fine). (c) flow.ts: add 'repair' to FlowActionType and the renderer; repair for asar-missing-backup-present and our-patch-without-backup should call restoreOriginal (not re-patch) so Discord is startable first, then re-inspect and continue the normal install path from 'unpatched'. On Windows check Discord is not running before the rename. Keep the reinstall refusal for asar-and-backup-missing. Also note a gap the finding misses: collectManaged (helper.ts:455-464) only manages a broken install when state.installs has its stableId, so a Discord whose helper never ran is skipped as 'not-ours'; the installer's repair action is then the only path, which makes (c) load-bearing, not optional.

title: A bundle left aside by an interrupted swap is neither recovered nor removed by uninstall, so a kept-for-safety stub points at a missing mod
scenario: Windows: removeScheduledTask runs schtasks /End (scheduledTask.ts:354) and kills a helper mid installModBundle between rename(destDir, old) and rename(staging, destDir): mod is absent, mod.subline-old holds the live bundle. Uninstall then runs: a target's restore fails (FILE_IN_USE), bundle 'kept for safety', but removeModBundle sees no mod dir (ok(false)) and nothing calls recoverModBundle. On a clean uninstall with keepSettings=true, mod.subline-old and mod.subline-staging stay in the product dir.
whatHappens: The still-patched Discord's stub requires mod/patcher.js which does not exist: a pre-0.2.1 one-line stub stops Discord starting, the fail-open stub silently loses translation, and the helper that would have recovered the bundle at login was just removed. Clean uninstalls leave megabytes behind.
fix: uninstall(): call recoverModBundle(modBundleDir) before the restore loop. removeModBundle: also remove `${dir}.subline-old` and `${dir}.subline-staging` when they carry our manifest.
test: installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts: only mod.subline-old present, one restore fails -> mod/patcher.js exists afterwards; clean uninstall removes both siblings. Fails today.
betterFix:
The proposed fix is right in direction but incomplete. Do this:

1. uninstall.ts: after the two preconditions and before the restore loop, call recoverModBundle(ports.modBundleDir) (platform-aware, pass the platform through). Log "uninstall.bundle-recovered" on true. If it returns an error, push it into problems and log "uninstall.bundle-recover-failed"; do NOT abort, the restores may still make the bundle unnecessary.

2. recoverModBundle (modInstall.ts): also handle "no `mod`, no `.subline-old`, but a `.subline-staging` that inspects OK". That state comes from a helper killed after cpSync but before rename on a repair install (replaced=false) while a stub already references `mod`. Promote it with the same renameWithRetry. Today the staging dir is only ever deleted by the NEXT install, so this is the only recovery for that state. After a successful recovery from `.subline-old`, rmSync the staging dir (it is a discarded new build).

3. removeModBundle (bundle.ts): after removing `mod`, also remove `${dir}.subline-old` and `${dir}.subline-staging`. Keep the manifest guard for `.subline-old` (it was a live bundle, so it always has one). Do NOT require a manifest for `.subline-staging`: an interrupted cpSync leaves a partial copy that may lack the manifest, and the suffix is Subline's own name under Subline's own product dir, so the "not ours" guard does not apply. Return ok(true) if any of the three was removed, so the report's modBundleRemoved is honest. Also delete the siblings in the modBundleKeptForSafety branch? No: `.subline-old` may be the only copy if recovery failed. Only remove `.subline-staging` there (never referenced by any stub).

4. summarize(): when !discordRestored and the bundle at modBundleDir does not exist after step 1 (recovery failed or nothing to recover), the sentence "Discord keeps working exactly as it does now" is false for a pre-0.2.1 stub. Say instead: "Discord may not start until Subline is reinstalled or Discord is reinstalled from discord.com", and include the recover error code. Pass a `bundlePresent` boolean into summarize.

5. Close the race the finding does not mention: removeScheduledTask's schtasks /End is not synchronous and the helper has no stillRegistered check inside installBundle. If uninstall's recovery renames `.subline-old` back while a still-dying helper then runs restoreOld (modInstall.ts:210-218), restoreOld rmSync's the recovered `mod` and the rename of the now-missing `.subline-old` fails: no bundle at all. Fix: after /End (Windows) and after bootout (macOS), poll until the helper process is gone (schtasks /Query /FO LIST Status != "Running", or ps/tasklist for the helper's executable) with a bounded wait of a few seconds before returning HelperRemoval; on timeout return an error so uninstall refuses with "Nothing has been changed" as it does for every other precondition.

Tests (installer/tests/uninstall.test.ts, each fails today):
- only `mod.subline-old` present, one restore returns FILE_IN_USE: `mod/patcher.js` exists afterwards, report.problems has no recover error, log has uninstall.bundle-recovered.
- only `mod.subline-staging` (complete, valid) present, one restore fails: `mod/patcher.js` exists afterwards.
- `mod.subline-old` present, recovery rename fails (fault seam or a file where the dir must go): problems contains the error and summary says Discord may not start.
- clean uninstall, keepSettings=true, `mod.subline-old` plus a manifest-less partial `mod.subline-staging`: both gone, modBundleRemoved=true.
- modInstallSwap.test.ts: recoverModBundle promotes a valid staging dir when neither `mod` nor `.subline-old` exist, and removes the staging dir after an `.subline-old` recovery.
- scheduledTask.test.ts / launchAgent.test.ts: removeScheduledTask/removeLaunchAgent wait until the helper reports not running; a helper that never stops yields an error, not ok(true).

title: macOS helper has no registration check: if launchctl print fails while the job is loaded, uninstall deletes the plist and the still-loaded helper re-downloads the bundle and re-patches Discord
