scenario: removeLaunchAgent: isLoaded() returns false whenever launchctl print exits non-zero (helper/ports.ts:208-215), so bootout is skipped and the plist is deleted; the job stays loaded until logout with WatchPaths on Discord's Resources. The uninstall's own rename starts the helper within 10 s. helper/ports.ts:423-425 provides stillRegistered only on win32, so helper.ts:952 and :611 never check. keepSettings=true leaves helper-state.json with the install remembered; bundle gone -> bundleUnusable -> maybeUpdate due -> download -> installBundle -> reconcile -> patchInstall.
whatHappens: Minutes after 'Discord has been put back to normal and Subline has been removed', the mod bundle is back and Discord is patched again, with a restart-required notification.
fix: helper/ports.ts: on darwin, stillRegistered = existsSync(launchAgentPlistPath(home)). removeLaunchAgent: when the plist exists, always attempt bootout (ignore 'not loaded') before deleting it, and report an error only when bootout fails for a loaded job.
test: installer/tests/helper.test.ts: platform darwin, stillRegistered -> false: no installBundle, no patch, no writeState. installer/tests/launchAgent.test.ts: isLoaded false but plist present -> bootout called once. Both fail today.
betterFix:
Keep both halves of the proposed fix, with these adjustments.

A. installer/src/helper/ports.ts (createHelperPorts): on darwin add `stillRegistered: async () => existsSync(launchAgentPlistPath(home))`. The plist is always written by temp+rename (installLaunchAgent and ensureHelperFromHelper), so there is no transient gap to misread. Make the "uninstalled" decision text in helper.ts:311 platform-neutral (today it says "the helper's scheduled task is gone").

B. installer/src/helper/launchAgent.ts removeLaunchAgent: do not gate bootout on isLoaded. If `wasLoaded || existsSync(plistPath)`, call bootout. If bootout fails, re-check `isLoaded`; return HELPER_REGISTRATION_FAILED and keep the plist only when it still reports loaded; otherwise treat the failure as "was not loaded" and continue to delete the plist. Return `ok(wasLoaded || booted.ok || existed)`. Part A is the backstop for the double-failure case (print and bootout both wrong).

C. Optional defence in depth, cheap: uninstall should drop `installs` from helper-state.json regardless of keepSettings (it is the helper's memory, not user settings; Vencord settings and the translation cache are what "keep settings" promises). Then even a rogue loaded job finds every Discord "not-ours" and cannot patch; with A it never gets that far.

Tests that fail today:
1. New installer/tests/helperPorts.test.ts (or in an existing ports test): `createHelperPorts({ platform: "darwin", home: tmpHome, searchRoots: [], releaseManifestUrl: null, ... })` -> `ports.stillRegistered` is defined; resolves false with no plist at `launchAgentPlistPath(tmpHome)`; resolves true after writing one. Fails today because the property is undefined on darwin.
2. installer/tests/launchAgent.test.ts: fakeLaunchctl with `loaded` cleared but plist present (reuse the "removes a plist left behind" setup) -> `launchctl.calls` contains exactly one `bootout gui/<uid>/<label>`; plist removed; result ok(true). Fails today (calls is empty). Add: fakeLaunchctl where isLoaded always returns false but the job is in `loaded` and bootout succeeds -> plist removed and `loaded` no longer has the label. Add: isLoaded false, bootout fails, isLoaded still false -> ok, plist removed (not-loaded failure ignored).
3. installer/tests/helper.test.ts darwin: patch for real, run once, delete the bundle dir and the fake plist-backed `stillRegistered` returns false, feed offers a build -> no installBundle, no patch, state file unchanged, report.uninstalled true. Note this one only fails today if the harness's `stillRegistered` is wired through the same existsSync predicate as A; wired as a bare `() => false` it already passes, so keep test 1 as the real red test.

title: The 'quit-required' remedy cannot work as worded: the repair needs Discord to stay closed across a 5-minute task boundary, and a user who quits and reopens at once is never repaired
scenario: 1. Discord was closed when Update.exe applied app-1.0.9260 at launch (no Vencord hook fires, since the old Subline was not running), so 9260 is genuinely unpatched and Discord now runs it without Subline. 2. Every 5-minute run: settle.ts:212 returns 'discord-running' at once (no waiting, settle.ts:105-112). 3. After 30 minutes the alert says 'choose Quit Discord, then open Discord again'. 4. The user quits and reopens within seconds, as told. The next run (up to 5 minutes later) finds Discord running again and defers. 5. Tomorrow the same alert repeats (alerts.ts DEFAULT_REPEAT_MS), with the same instruction, forever.
whatHappens: The user is stuck: they do exactly what Subline asks and nothing changes, which reads as 'Subline is broken'. Field evidence of the mechanism: diagnostics.txt lines 1480-1525, nine consecutive deferred runs across two days because Discord was always running when the task fired.
fix: Minimum: change the copy to 'Quit Discord and leave it closed for a few minutes. Subline puts itself back while it is closed, then open Discord again.' Better: when and only when a repair is pending and the only blocker is a running Discord, let that run poll ports.discordRunning every 10 s for up to 4 minutes (inside the task's PT10M ExecutionTimeLimit, scheduledTask.ts:157) and patch the moment Discord exits, so the repair lands within seconds of the quit. Idle runs (nothing pending) keep the single look, so the cost objection in settle.ts:105-112 does not apply. Alternatively register a second, event-driven trigger on Discord.exe process termination; the poll is simpler and testable.
test: tests/helper.test.ts, platform win32: fixture with injection wiped, discordOpen true; make discordRunning flip to false after the 3rd call within one run; expect report.repatched to contain the install in that same run and deferred to be empty. Second test: harness with nothing to repair must call discordRunning at most once per run (the cheap path is preserved). Third: the quit-required alert message must contain 'leave it closed' (copy test in tests/alerts.test.ts or copy.test.ts).
betterFix: The problem is real but the proposed fix is incomplete and its cost claim is wrong. (1) The claim "idle runs keep the single look so the cost objection does not apply" fails on the field case itself: the repair was PENDING for days with Discord in the tray, so a 4 minute poll in every 5 minute run would keep the Electron helper (main.ts isHelperRun) resident ~80% of the time indefinitely, which is exactly what the settle.ts:105-112 note removed. (2) A 4 minute poll in a 5 minute interval leaves a ~1 minute blind gap per cycle, so a quick quit+reopen can still be missed. Better: a) Change the copy regardless: "Quit Discord and leave it closed for a minute. Subline puts itself back while it is closed, then open Discord again." b) Poll only while a repair is pending AND the quit-required alert has just been shown: for the first N runs (say 6 runs = 30 minutes) after each quit-required notification, let awaitDiscordSettled wait for Discord to exit with a 10 s discordRunning check for up to ~4m45s (inside ExecutionTimeLimit PT10M, under the PT5M interval so IgnoreNew never drops a run), and patch the moment it exits; all other runs keep the single look. The user is most likely to act right after the toast, so this covers the real window without a resident helper all day. c) Since the repair lands within ~10 s of the quit, no "you can reopen now" notice is needed; keep the existing quitAnswered suppression. d) Tests: win32 fixture with injection wiped, discordOpen=true, run until quit-required fires, then make discordRunning flip to false on the 3rd call within the next run and expect repatched to contain the install in that run; a run with nothing pending must call discordRunning at most once; a run 30+ minutes after the alert with Discord still open must make at most 2 checks (cheap path restored); copy test for "leave it closed". Neighbour to cover in the same pass: Discord autostarts at logon on Windows, so the LogonTrigger run also races a starting Discord and usually finds it running; the post-alert poll does not help there, so the logon run should also be allowed one bounded wait when a repair is pending.

title: Root cause of the lost Windows marker: the bundled Vencord re-injects the stub into the new app-x.y.z folder from inside Discord and never carries subline-patch.json
scenario: 1. Subline patches app-1.0.9258 (stub, _app.asar, subline-patch.json). 2. Discord downloads a host update and installs app-1.0.9259 while still running 9258 with Subline loaded. 3. Either Discord emits 'host-updated' or the user quits Discord: Vencord's patchLatest() (shipped inside Subline's patcher.js, confirmed by grep of installer/build/mod/patcher.js: 'Detected Host Update ... renameSync(a,u),copyFileSync(i,a)') renames 9259/resources/app.asar to _app.asar and copies 9258's app.asar (Subline's stub) over it. It does not copy subline-patch.json (patcher.js contains the string 'subline-patch' zero times). 4. Next helper run: inspectInstall -> classifyStub (src/patcher/state.ts:251) sees stub + backup, marker null -> identifyModFromLoaderPath -> 'unknown' -> patched-by-other -> helper logs 'foreign-mod' and abandons (helper.ts:471-479); uninstall refuses with FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT (patch.ts:469-476). This matches diagnostics.txt lines 1530, 1545-1577, 1586, 1600 exactly, and explains why no Subline log line precedes the stub's appearance in either gap (it was written by Discord's process).
whatHappens: Translation actually keeps working (Vencord's copy is a working Subline stub), but the helper stops managing the install forever, every later Discord update repeats the copy without a marker, the installer shows 'another client mod' with a 'Replace it' button over Subline's own stub, and uninstall fails with FOREIGN_MOD_PRESENT and keeps the bundle. The owner's machine runs app 0.1.3 with mod 0.2.1 (diagnostics header), so a fix that lives only in the app's classifier never reaches installs that update through the mod feed; the marker must survive the copy as well.
fix: Two parts. (a) Keep the classifier fix in progress (a stub whose loader is Subline's own bundle path is ours regardless of marker; helper re-adopts and writes the marker). (b) Make the marker travel with the stub, in the mod bundle so it reaches old apps through the feed: in installer/scripts/buildMod.mjs use the existing anchored replace() helper (buildMod.mjs:403-407) to rewrite persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts so that after copyFileSync(oldVencordAsar, newAppAsar) it also copies join(oldResources, 'subline-patch.json') to join(resources, 'subline-patch.json') when present (copyFileSync inside the same try). Optionally also rewrite the marker's discordVersion from the new folder's build_info.json, but the helper's own memory already covers version detection. Keep the hook (it is what keeps translation alive across a Windows host update without waiting for Discord to close); do not disable it.
test: 1. tests/persistAcrossHostUpdate.test.ts: after buildMod's rewrite step, read installer/build/mod/patcher.js (or run the rewrite on the pinned source text in isolation) and assert the host-update block copies 'subline-patch.json' next to 'Detected Host Update'; the assertion fails against unmodified Vencord. 2. tests/state.test.ts: Windows-shaped fixture with app-1.0.9258 (patched by us) and app-1.0.9259 (genuine); simulate Vencord's copy exactly (rename new app.asar -> _app.asar, copy old app.asar, no marker); inspectInstall(9259) must report kind patched-by-us with mod 'subline', and runHelperOnce with the 9258 stableId remembered must write subline-patch.json into 9259 and report it repatched, not 'foreign-mod'. 3. tests/uninstall.test.ts: same fixture; uninstallTargets + unpatchInstall must restore both folders and remove the bundle.
betterFix:
1. buildMod.mjs:403 replace() is a closure over settings.tsx's `source`; it cannot be reused for another file. Hoist a generic rewriteSource(relPath, what, from, to) (exactly-one-anchor, fail() otherwise) into a small importable module (e.g. installer/scripts/vencordPatches.mjs) and apply it to src/main/persistAfterDiscordUpdates.ts. Anchor on the two-line block `renameSync(newAppAsar, newAppAsarBackup);\n        copyFileSync(oldVencordAsar, newAppAsar);` so a pin bump that moves the code fails the build instead of silently shipping without the marker.
2. Do not copy the marker verbatim. Copying leaves discordVersion = old folder and backupPath = old folder's _app.asar (no code reads marker.backupPath today, but the helper then logs discord-version-changed and schedules a full repatch that defers forever while Discord runs). In the hook, after the asar copy succeeds and in its OWN try/catch so a marker failure can never undo or block the stub copy: read oldResources/subline-patch.json if it exists, JSON.parse, set discordVersion from join(resources, 'build_info.json').version when readable (else keep old), set backupPath = newAppAsarBackup, patchedAt = now, write to join(resources, 'subline-patch.json'); if parsing fails, fall back to copyFileSync of the raw file. Use original-fs like the rest of the file. Leave pluginBuildId as is (the helper's adopt/repatch path reconciles it).
3. Tests go in installer/tests/, not tests/. Unit-test the rewrite function on the pinned source text (no network): assert the output contains the marker write after the asar copy, and assert it throws on text without the anchor. Add a fixture test in state.test.ts/helper.test.ts that simulates the hook's result WITH the carried marker (stub + _app.asar + marker naming the new backupPath) and asserts patched-by-us with no warnings and uninstall restoring both folders; keep the existing marker-less case from foreignMarker.test.ts as the 'old bundle' path.
4. Say in the release note that the owner's current app-1.0.9260 is already marker-less, so (b) cannot repair it; only the app build carrying (a), or a reinstall, takes it back. Also keep the hook enabled (Subline never sets DISABLE_UPDATER_AUTO_PATCHING), because it is what keeps translation alive across a Windows host update while the helper is deferred by a running Discord.

title: Helper abandons a fresh install if Discord updates before the helper's first run: ownership is read only from helper-state.json, never from patched-installs.json or sibling residue, and Windows never runs the task immediately
scenario: Windows worst case: 1. Installer patches app-1.0.9258, writes only patched-installs.json (flow.ts:1797 -> main/ports.ts:705) and registers the task (main/ports.ts:208-229; no 'schtasks /Run', TimeTrigger repeats every 5 min, scheduledTask.ts:136-143). helper-state.json has no 'installs' entry yet (only runHelperOnce writes it, helper.ts:341-343). 2. The flow launches Discord; Update.exe applies a pending host update at launch and Discord starts from app-1.0.9259. 3. First helper run (up to 5 min later): locate() picks 9259 (newest), inspect -> unpatched, no marker, run.state.installs[stableId] undefined -> 'not-ours: Subline has never patched this install' (helper.ts:452-457) and found=1 managed=0 every run thereafter. diagnostics.txt lines 194-215 and 1431 show this exact log shape in the field after every update. macOS: same window, shorter (RunAtLoad fires at registration), but a Discord that swaps its bundle between the patch and the first agent run is identical.
whatHappens: Subline silently stops working after the very first Discord update and the helper never repairs it; the installer's 'already installed' check also fails (no marker) so reopening the app walks a full install. The helper is abandoning an install it owns, which violates the product rule, and the stub+backup+marker left in the old app-1.0.9258 folder is found only by uninstall.
fix: In collectManaged: oursOnce = remembered !== undefined || rememberedStableIds (from readPatchedInstalls, passed in as a port) has install.stableId || (win32 only) any sibling app-* dir under dirname(install.rootPath) carries our mark (reuse locatePatchedResidue / carriesOurMark on the branch dir). Add HelperPorts.rememberedStableIds(): Set<string> wired to readPatchedInstalls(productDir). Also seed helper memory at install time: after a successful patch the flow (or FlowPorts.rememberPatchedInstall) writes installs[stableId] = { discordVersion, buildId, patchedAt } via writeHelperState so the first helper run already knows. On Windows, after installScheduledTask succeeds, run 'schtasks /Run /TN \Subline\Helper' once (ignore failure) so memory and WatchPaths-equivalent coverage exist within seconds, not 5 minutes.
test: tests/helper.test.ts: new case 'adopts an install remembered only by patched-installs.json after a Windows version bump'. Harness with EMPTY helper state, patched-installs.json listing the fixture's stableId, fixture moved to a new app-1.0.<n+1> folder with a genuine app.asar and no marker (simulateDiscordUpdate + new rootPath, as the existing Windows bump test does). Expect report.managed === 1 and report.repatched to contain the new rootPath; without the fix managed === 0 (the existing 'ignores a Discord Subline has never patched' test must still pass with no memory anywhere). Second case: old folder carries residue (marker + backup), helper state empty, patched-installs.json absent -> still adopted. Third: flow.test.ts asserts a successful patch leaves helper-state.json with installs[stableId] populated.
betterFix: The proposed fix is correct in direction; tighten it this way. 1) Primary witness: treat patched-installs.json as ownership, not just as a locate hint. Add HelperPorts.rememberedStableIds(): ReadonlySet<string> wired to readPatchedInstalls(productDir) (helper/ports.ts already imports it); in collectManaged set oursOnce = remembered !== undefined || rememberedStableIds.has(install.stableId). Keep the kind checks after it so a remembered install that is now patched-by-other still takes the foreign-mod branch, and the other-account check still applies. 2) Residue witness, win32 only, scoped to install.stableId (the branch dir), never dirname(rootPath) of a hand-picked unversioned root: any findWindowsAppDirs(install.stableId) entry whose makeInstall carriesOurMark (reuse locate.ts:390-397 logic via a port, e.g. HelperPorts.siblingCarriesOurMark(install)).
